marketplace.name: ai-foundry
marketplace.description: The AI Foundry (BYU Marriott) toolbox for building your own Claude Code harness: an 8-stage SDLC framework plus skills, agents and hooks, each labeled proven (runs in production in our harness) or new (written for this marketplace).

stages.name: Scaffold
stages.goal: the project has the full artifact set, so every later stage has a place to write.
stages.gate: all files exist. `stories.json` is compiled from the new PRD, so `python3 tools/gen_stories.py --check` passes right away.
stages.artifact: README.md, REQUIREMENTS.md, DECISIONS.md, PRD.md, WORKPLAN.md, CHANGELOG.md, stories.json, stories.schema.json, done-journey.yaml, plus `tools/gen_stories.py`. Templates: `templates/*`.

stages.name: Requirements
stages.goal: know exactly what was asked, by whom, and what already exists.
stages.gate: every ask is verbatim with an R-id and a source. The "Already exists" audit is filled. No `TODO` markers remain.
stages.artifact: `REQUIREMENTS.md` (template `templates/REQUIREMENTS.md`) with each ask verbatim and an R-id (R-01, R-02...) plus its source and date, and `DECISIONS.md` (template `templates/DECISIONS.md`) with human decisions recorded verbatim.

stages.name: PRD + stories
stages.goal: a PRD whose stories can be checked by someone who did not write them.
stages.gate: stories have observable criteria. The `prd-critic` agent's critiques are addressed in Appendix A. `gen_stories.py --check` exits 0. Every R-id's Status in REQUIREMENTS.md is `STORIED` (or `LIVE`), or `DROPPED` citing the D-id that dropped it. DECISIONS.md has the human's dated `PRD approved` row in their own words. Approval is never inferred; after it, stop until the human asks for the workplan.
stages.artifact: `PRD.md` (template `templates/PRD.md`) with inline stories in the form `**US-01. Title.**` followed by numbered, observable acceptance criteria, and `stories.json` compiled from it (schema `templates/stories.schema.json`). Never hand-edit a title or a criterion in stories.json; only `status`, `notes` and `evidence` are edited there.

stages.name: Workplan
stages.goal: a plan that agents can execute in parallel and humans can read in one minute.
stages.gate: every task has an owner, model, effort and review tier. Milestones exist. The "Blocked on human" list exists.
stages.artifact: `WORKPLAN.md` (template `templates/WORKPLAN.md`): a task table `Id | Task | Owner | Deps | Status` where Owner names the model, effort and review tier, plus milestone checkboxes (`- [ ] M1.1 title`), "Next up", and "Blocked on human".

stages.name: Execute
stages.goal: build each task in isolation, then merge it back.
stages.gate: every task is PARKED, or DONE with evidence in its Status cell (`DONE 2026-11-03: commit 3f2a9c1`, a PR `#12` or a URL).
stages.artifact: code, one branch per lane (`lane/<task-id>-<slug>`), one worktree per lane (`../<repo>-lanes/<task-id>`), one PR per lane.

stages.name: Code QA
stages.goal: the code does what the tests say, and nothing downstream broke.
stages.gate: each change has a test. The blast radius of shared changes was checked. CI is green.

stages.name: Visual QA with example users
stages.goal: the build under test works for real kinds of users on the devices they use.
stages.gate: `last.json` says exit 0 for git HEAD (or for a commit whose only later changes are artifact files), and every story that is not PARKED has a verifier report or evidence. INCONCLUSIVE is not a pass.
stages.artifact: `done-journey.yaml` (template `templates/done-journey.yaml`), the done gate's `.qa/done-gate/last.json` (`sha`, `exit`, `journey`, `time`), one story-verifier report per story (`.qa/verify/<id>.md`), screenshots, persona reports.

stages.name: Ship
stages.goal: users know what they can now do, and the record says what is LIVE and why.
stages.gate: every story that is not PARKED is LIVE with `commit:<sha>` evidence, and the changelog has a dated entry. Order: the gate passed, then the changelog, then the users were told what to try. Never in the other order.
stages.artifact: `CHANGELOG.md` (template `templates/CHANGELOG.md`) with a dated entry, and story status `LIVE` with `evidence` in stories.json. Set LIVE only with `tools/gen_stories.py --set US-01=LIVE --evidence .qa/verify/US-01.md`: it refuses a dirty tracked tree, a missing or failing done-gate report for HEAD, and a story with no evidence, and it appends `commit:<sha>` to the story's evidence.

stages.name: Feedback
stages.goal: every bug makes the system stronger, and features graduate on evidence.
stages.gate: each bug has a story and a test that fails before the fix. A human decides when a feature graduates.
stages.artifact: new R-ids and stories (or criteria) in the PRD, and regression tests that fail before the fix.

plugins.name: foundry-sdlc
plugins.description: The 8-stage 0-to-1 workflow: scaffold, requirements, PRD and stories, workplan, parallel lanes, QA, ship, feedback. Templates, a PRD-to-stories compiler, a stage detector, and two independent judge agents (prd-critic, story-verifier).
plugins.readme:
# foundry-sdlc

The deterministic 0-to-1 workflow AI Foundry uses to take software from an idea to a shipped, verified product with Claude Code agents. It has eight stages. Each stage produces one file and ends at a gate. A stage detector tells any agent which stage a project is in, so a new session (or a new teammate) picks up exactly where the last one stopped.

| # | Stage | Artifact | Item in this plugin |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Scaffold | the artifact set | `new-project` skill, `skills/new-project/scripts/new_project.py` |
| 1 | Gather requirements | `REQUIREMENTS.md`, `DECISIONS.md` | `gather-requirements` skill |
| 2 | PRD + user stories | `PRD.md`, `stories.json` | `write-prd` skill, `scripts/gen_stories.py`, `prd-critic` agent |
| 3 | Workplan | `WORKPLAN.md` | `write-workplan` skill |
| 4 | Execute | branches, one per lane | `parallel-lanes` skill |
| 5 | Code QA | tests, CI | (companion: `foundry-qa` regression-check) |
| 6 | Visual QA with example users | `done-journey.yaml`, `.qa/done-gate/last.json`, `.qa/verify/<id>.md` | the battery in the `sdlc` and `ship` skills: `story-verifier` agent plus `foundry-qa` (done-gate, persona-tester, a11y-check) and `foundry-design` (design-critique); `foundry-devices` for native apps |
| 7 | Ship | `CHANGELOG.md`, stories LIVE | `ship` skill |
| 8 | Feedback | new stories + failing tests | `bug-to-story` skill (companion: `foundry-evals`) |

The `sdlc` skill is the router. It holds the full map and the one rule that matters most: **never skip a gate**.

## Install

Add the marketplace once:

```text
/plugin marketplace add ai-foundry-byu/foundry-marketplace
```

Install this plugin:

```text
/plugin install foundry-sdlc@ai-foundry
```

From a shell instead (for example, to install for the whole project):

```bash
claude plugin install foundry-sdlc@ai-foundry --scope project
```

The companion plugins are installed the same way: `foundry-guardrails`, `foundry-qa`, `foundry-design`, `foundry-devices`, `foundry-evals`.

## Quick start

In your project, ask Claude: "Use foundry-sdlc to start a new project called Study Buddy." Or do it by hand, from the project root (leave out `--name` to take it from the folder name):

```bash
python3 "$PLUGIN/skills/new-project/scripts/new_project.py" product --name "<Project Name>" --owner "<Owner>"
```

```bash
python3 tools/gen_stories.py --prd product/PRD.md --out product/stories.json --check
```

```bash
python3 "$PLUGIN/skills/sdlc/scripts/sdlc_stage.py" .
```

(`$PLUGIN` is the plugin's install directory, `$HOME/.claude/plugins/cache/ai-foundry/foundry-sdlc/<version>/`, or your clone of this repo at `plugins/foundry-sdlc`.) The scaffolder writes the artifacts to `product/`, and `tools/gen_stories.py` plus `.github/workflows/stories.yml` to the project root (the git root). The story check passes right after scaffolding. Then paste `skills/new-project/references/CLAUDE-md-snippet.md` into your project's `CLAUDE.md`.

**Shipping without hosting.** A class project needs no deploy: the build under test is the app started locally from the committed HEAD. What it does need is a commit. `gen_stories.py --set US-01=LIVE` refuses a dirty tree, a missing or failing done-gate report for HEAD, and a story with no evidence.

## Install one item on its own

Every skill in this plugin is self-contained: the scripts, templates and references it runs or copies live inside its own folder and are addressed as `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/...`. So you can copy one skill folder into `.claude/skills/<name>/` (one project) or `~/.claude/skills/<name>/` (all projects) without the rest of the plugin.

| Item | On its own? | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `sdlc`, `gather-requirements`, `write-prd`, `write-workplan`, `parallel-lanes`, `ship` | standalone | Each carries its own copy of `scripts/sdlc_stage.py` and its helper `scripts/gen_stories.py` |
| `new-project` | standalone | Carries `scripts/new_project.py`, `scripts/gen_stories.py` (copied to `tools/` at the project root), `scripts/sdlc_stage.py`, all of `templates/` and `references/CLAUDE-md-snippet.md` |
| `bug-to-story` | standalone | Runs only the project's own `tools/gen_stories.py`, so it ships no files |
| `prd-critic`, `story-verifier` agents | standalone | Copy the `.md` into `.claude/agents/` or `~/.claude/agents/`. Neither runs a plugin script, so neither needs a skill |
| SessionStart stage hint | plugin only | Hooks need the plugin's `hooks/hooks.json` |

When run on their own, the skills are named `sdlc`, `write-prd` and so on, without the `foundry-sdlc:` prefix.

**Single source of truth.** Files used by several skills have one canonical copy and byte-identical copies in the other skills, listed in `vendor.json` (copy path: canonical path). `scripts/sdlc_stage.py` and `scripts/gen_stories.py` stay at the plugin root because the hook runs them there. The CLAUDE.md snippet's canonical copy is in `new-project`. Edit the canonical file, then re-copy it: `scripts/tests/test_layout.py` fails when a copy drifts.

## Items

### Skills

Invoke a skill by asking in plain words, for example "write the PRD", or by name: `/foundry-sdlc:write-prd`.

| Skill | What it does | Maturity |
|---|---|---|
| `sdlc` | The router. Stage map, which artifact and which skill or agent each stage uses, how to detect the current stage, the single-session build path, and the stage-6 battery ("check that it really works end to end") | proven |
| `new-project` | Scaffolds the artifact set from its `templates/`, compiles `stories.json` from the new PRD, and writes `tools/gen_stories.py` and the CI check at the project root. Derives the name from the folder when none is given | proven |
| `gather-requirements` | Verbatim asks with R-ids and sources, a DECISIONS table, and an "Already exists" audit before the PRD | proven |
| `write-prd` | The PRD with inline `**US-01. Title.**` stories and observable criteria. Compiles stories.json, runs the prd-critic, fills "Addressed critiques", and on the human's yes records a dated `PRD approved` D-row and stops | proven |
| `write-workplan` | Task table (Id, Task, Owner with model, effort and review tier by blast radius, Deps, Status), milestones, "Blocked on human" | proven |
| `parallel-lanes` | One git worktree and one agent per independent task: naming, the lane brief, the "edit only inside your worktree" rule, merge back. Also the single-session path. Either way each task goes `DONE <date>: commit <sha>` as it lands | proven (lanes); single-session path new |
| `ship` | The ship ritual: commit, then done gate, persona testers, one story-verifier per story, design critique and a11y on that commit (local or hosted), all in the foreground; LIVE only through the guarded `--set`; changelog; "go try X" | proven (ritual); local path and LIVE guard new |
| `bug-to-story` | Every bug report (also "a classmate says X is broken") becomes an R-id, a story criterion, a failing regression test, a task and a changelog line. Usage gates, with graduation decided by a human | proven |

### Agents

| Agent | What it does | Maturity |
|---|---|---|
| `prd-critic` | Adversarial PRD review in a fresh context. Returns numbered critiques (C1..) with severity, location and a suggested fix. Read-only: never rewrites the PRD | proven (pattern) |
| `story-verifier` | Checks one story on the build under test (deployed or local) from its criteria, the URL and screenshots only. One per story, before anything is marked LIVE. Returns PASS, FAIL or INCONCLUSIVE per criterion with evidence. Never reads the builder's claims | proven (pattern) |

Use them by asking, for example "Use the prd-critic agent on product/PRD.md", or let the `write-prd` and `ship` skills call them.

### Hook

| Hook | What it does | Maturity |
|---|---|---|
| SessionStart stage hint | Runs `sdlc_stage.py --hook`. If the project has a `PRD.md` or `REQUIREMENTS.md` (in the root, `product/` or `docs/product/`), it prints two lines: the current stage and the failing exit check. Silent otherwise. It never blocks a session | new |

### Scripts

| Script | What it does | Maturity |
|---|---|---|
| `scripts/gen_stories.py` (canonical; copied into each skill that runs the detector) | Compiles PRD stories into `stories.json`, shape `{"stories": [...]}` (contract C1, shared with `foundry-qa`). `--check` exits 1 if the file is stale (or the old bare-array format), a story has no criteria, an id is duplicated, or a status is invalid. Regenerating keeps `status`, `notes`, `evidence`, a `qa` block, extra keys and any meta the PRD does not set. `--set US-01=LIVE --evidence <path>` refuses LIVE unless the tree is committed and the done-gate report says exit 0 for HEAD, and records `commit:<sha>` | proven (compiler, generalized port); `--set` guard new |
| `skills/new-project/scripts/new_project.py` | Scaffolds the artifact set, compiles `stories.json`, writes `tools/` and `.github/workflows/stories.yml` at the project root. Never overwrites without `--force` | new |
| `scripts/sdlc_stage.py` (canonical; used by the hook, copied into each skill that runs it) | Reports the current stage from the files on disk (`--json` for machines, `--hook` for the SessionStart hook). Stage 2 needs every R-id STORIED or `DROPPED (D-xx)` and a dated `PRD approved` D-row; stage 4 needs every task DONE with a sha, PR or URL, or PARKED; stage 6 needs `.qa/done-gate/last.json` with exit 0 for HEAD and a `.qa/verify/<id>.md` per story; stage 7 needs every LIVE story to carry `commit:<sha>` evidence | new |

### Templates and references

All templates live in `skills/new-project/templates/`, since only the scaffolder uses them.

| File | Purpose | Maturity |
|---|---|---|
| `skills/new-project/templates/REQUIREMENTS.md` | Sources, verbatim asks (R-01..), "Already exists" audit, constraints, open questions | proven |
| `skills/new-project/templates/DECISIONS.md` | Verbatim human decisions with what each one authorizes, and pending questions with a recommendation | proven |
| `skills/new-project/templates/PRD.md` | Short version, user, metrics, principles, scope, stories, architecture, rollout with "used fully" gates, risks, Appendix A (addressed critiques), Appendix B (push back) | proven |
| `skills/new-project/templates/WORKPLAN.md` | Status block, blast-radius tiers, Next up, milestones, task table, Blocked on human, Parked | proven |
| `skills/new-project/templates/stories.schema.json` | JSON Schema for stories.json: `{"stories": [{id, title, acceptance[], surfaces[], devices[], status, waits_on[], covers[], notes, evidence[], optional qa}]}` | proven |
| `skills/new-project/templates/done-journey.yaml` | Byte-identical copy of `foundry-qa`'s canonical `skills/done-gate/templates/done-journey.yaml` (contract C2): `name`, `base_url`, `devices`, `stories`, optional `auth`, `steps`, `assertions`, `screenshot`. A test checks it matches and passes `done_gate.py --validate` | proven (format) |
| `skills/new-project/templates/stories-ci.yml` | GitHub Actions job that runs `python3 tools/gen_stories.py --prd <PRD> --out <stories> --check`; the scaffolder fills in the paths | new |
| `skills/new-project/templates/CHANGELOG.md` | One dated heading per ship, one bullet per user-visible change, with evidence | proven |
| `skills/new-project/templates/README.md` | Project README that indexes the artifact set | new |
| `skills/new-project/references/CLAUDE-md-snippet.md` (copied into `sdlc`) | Always-on norms to paste into a project CLAUDE.md: every bug report through `bug-to-story`, root cause first, surgical changes, never "done" without passing gates on a committed SHA, the 4-tier blast-radius table, reuse before build | proven |

**What the maturity labels mean.** "proven" means the item is generalized from a workflow, format or tool that runs in production in our harness today. "proven (pattern)" means the agent's role and rules are what we use in production, rewritten here as a portable agent definition. "new" means it was written for this marketplace and is not yet battle-tested. Please report problems.

## Requirements

- Claude Code with plugin support.
- Python 3.8 or later for the scripts (standard library only).
- git 2.5 or later for worktrees (`parallel-lanes`).
- For `story-verifier` to drive a browser: Playwright for Python (`pip install playwright`, then `python3 -m playwright install chromium`). Without it, the verifier judges from screenshots and HTTP checks, and marks the rest INCONCLUSIVE.
- For stages 5 and 6: the companion plugins `foundry-qa` (done-gate, persona-tester, regression-check) and `foundry-design`. Native apps need `foundry-devices`.

## Tests

```bash
cd plugins/foundry-sdlc && python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -v
```

## Related work

Scott Murff's **agent-team-kit** (https://github.com/ai-foundry-byu/agent-team-kit) is a complementary team harness. It covers spec, mockup, build-spec, worktree launchers, merge-worktree, a regression check and release skills, installed with its own `install.sh`. This plugin does not copy any of its files. See its repository for license and usage.

## License

MIT. Copyright AI Foundry (BYU Marriott).

plugins.name: foundry-guardrails
plugins.description: Hooks that make the gates real: block destructive commands and secret leaks, require tests before done and before push or deploy, keep worktree sessions in their worktree, flag stale whole-file writes, and keep working until a workplan milestone is checked.
plugins.readme:
# foundry-guardrails

Claude Code hooks that turn SDLC rules from advice into gates. Your system prompt can *ask* Claude to run tests before saying "done", to stay out of `.env`, or to never force-push `main`. A hook *checks* it on every tool call and every stop, and it keeps checking when the session runs with skipped permission prompts.

Six hooks, all Python 3 standard library, all on by default except `ship-stop` (which turns on when you point it at a workplan):

| Hook | Event (matcher) | What it blocks | Default | Disable | Maturity |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `destructive-guard` | PreToolUse (`Bash`) | `rm -rf` of `/`, `~`, `$HOME`, `*`, `.` or a system dir; force-push to `main`/`master` (plain `--force` anywhere); `git reset --hard`, `git checkout -- .`, `git restore .`, `git clean -f` when they would destroy uncommitted work; `DROP`/`TRUNCATE`/`DELETE` without `WHERE` sent through a DB client; `dd of=/dev/...`; `mkfs`; fork bombs; `chmod -R 777 /`; `curl ... \| sh`; `shutdown`/`reboot` | deny | `FOUNDRY_DESTRUCTIVE_GUARD=0` | new |
| `secret-guard` | PreToolUse (`Bash\|Read\|Grep`) | Reading or printing `.env`, private keys, cloud/registry credential files; browser password and cookie stores; password-manager CLIs (`bw`, `op`, `lpass`, `pass`, `security ... -w`); token printers (`gh auth token`, `gcloud auth print-access-token`, ...); `env`/`printenv` dumps; `echo $API_KEY`. Listing key names only (`cut -d= -f1 .env`) is allowed | deny | `FOUNDRY_SECRET_GUARD=0` | proven |
| `verify-before-done` | PreToolUse (`Bash\|Edit\|Write\|MultiEdit\|NotebookEdit`) + Stop | Stopping after changing code with no test or typecheck run since the change (blocks once per stop, at most 2 times per session). In a git repo it detects the change by content, so edits made with `sed -i`, heredocs, `tee`, `cp` or a script count too. Irreversible commands (`git push`, `vercel --prod`, `npm publish`, `wrangler deploy`, `terraform apply`, `gh pr merge`, ...) unless the command contains `VERIFY_OK=1`, which is refused while code is untested | on | `FOUNDRY_VERIFY=0` | proven (the Edit/Write path); the shell-edit detection is new |
| `worktree-guard` | PreToolUse (`Edit\|Write\|MultiEdit\|NotebookEdit`) | From inside a linked git worktree, editing a file in the main checkout | deny (only acts inside a linked worktree) | `FOUNDRY_WORKTREE_GUARD=0` | proven |
| `stale-write-guard` | PreToolUse (`Write`) + PostToolUse (`Edit\|Write\|MultiEdit`) | A whole-file `Write` to a git-tracked file whose uncommitted changes were not made by this session (they would be overwritten) | deny (`FOUNDRY_STALE_WRITE_ENFORCE=0` warns instead) | `FOUNDRY_STALE_WRITE_GUARD=0` | new |
| `ship-stop` | Stop | Stopping while the workplan milestone you named is still `- [ ]` (at most 8 continuations per milestone) | off until `FOUNDRY_SHIP_WORKPLAN` is set | `FOUNDRY_SHIP_STOP=0` or unset the workplan | proven |
| `guardrails-help` | skill | Tells Claude how to respond when a guardrail blocks it, and tells you how to configure the hooks | n/a | n/a | new |

`FOUNDRY_GUARDRAILS=0` turns every hook off at once.

**Maturity.** "proven" means the hook is a generalized version of a hook that runs in our own Claude Code harness every day. "new" means it was written for this marketplace from documented patterns and is tested here, but it has not been run in daily use. `destructive-guard` uses the rule set of the published `claude-deploy-kit` command guard (a library, not a hook), so it is labeled new. `stale-write-guard` is ported from a guard we wrote but never switched on, and its deny-by-default design (2026-10-28) has unit tests but no live session yet, so it is labeled new too.

## Guardrails, not a security boundary

These hooks catch the mistakes a well-meaning agent actually makes: running `cat .env` to "check the config", force-pushing over a teammate, wiping a directory with a bad glob, declaring victory without running tests. They are **not** a sandbox. A determined process can get around any pattern list. Scripts that read secrets from inside a file and commands built at runtime are invisible to them, and only `verify-before-done` sees shell writes such as `cat > file` (by their effect on the files; `worktree-guard` and `stale-write-guard` watch only the edit tools). For a real boundary, use OS-level isolation: a container or VM, a scrubbed environment with no secrets in it, and least-privilege credentials. Use both.

## Install

Add the marketplace:

```text
/plugin marketplace add ai-foundry-byu/foundry-marketplace
```

Install the plugin:

```text
/plugin install foundry-guardrails@ai-foundry
```

Restart Claude Code so the hooks load. Then confirm they are registered:

```text
/hooks
```

To try it from a local clone without installing:

```bash
claude --plugin-dir ./plugins/foundry-guardrails
```

### Install one item on its own

Nothing in this plugin works on its own. The six guardrails are hooks, and only a plugin can install hooks (they live in `hooks/hooks.json` and point at `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/scripts/`).

| Item | Standalone copy? | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| all six hooks | no, plugin only | the plugin install |
| `guardrails-help` skill | no, plugin only | the hooks it explains. It references no files, so a copy in `.claude/skills/` loads, but without the hooks there is nothing for it to explain |

There are no agents in this plugin.

## Requirements

- `python3` (3.8 or newer) on your `PATH`. The hooks run in exec form (`python3 <script>`), so there is no shell quoting to break. If `python3` is missing, Claude Code treats each hook as a non-blocking error and the tool call goes ahead, so you lose the guard but your session keeps working.
- `git` for `destructive-guard` (dirty-tree checks), `worktree-guard` and `stale-write-guard`.
- macOS or Linux. Windows works when `python3` resolves to a real executable. Nothing here is tested on Windows yet.

## Configuration

Every switch is an environment variable. Put them in the `env` block of `.claude/settings.json` (project, shared with your team) or `.claude/settings.local.json` (just you), so the agent cannot change them from inside a command:

```json
{
  "env": {
    "FOUNDRY_VERIFY_IGNORE": "*.json,*.lock",
    "FOUNDRY_SHIP_WORKPLAN": "WORKPLAN.md",
    "FOUNDRY_SHIP_MILESTONE": "M3.2"
  }
}
```

| Variable | Hook | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `FOUNDRY_GUARDRAILS=0` | all | disable every hook |
| `FOUNDRY_DESTRUCTIVE_GUARD=0` | destructive-guard | disable |
| `FOUNDRY_DESTRUCTIVE_ALLOW=rule1,rule2` | destructive-guard | allow named rules for the session (rule names appear in every deny message, for example `git-reset-hard`) |
| `FOUNDRY_ALLOW_FORCE_PUSH=1` | destructive-guard | allow plain `--force` to non-protected branches. `main`/`master` stay blocked |
| `FOUNDRY_PROTECTED_BRANCHES=develop,release` | destructive-guard | add protected branches (`main` and `master` are always protected) |
| `FOUNDRY_SECRET_GUARD=0` | secret-guard | disable. The foundry-builder-kit commit guard is a separate hook with its own switch, `FOUNDRY_COMMIT_SECRET_GUARD=0` |
| `FOUNDRY_VERIFY=0` | verify-before-done | disable (also the human override when a push must go out unverified) |
| `FOUNDRY_VERIFY_MAX_BLOCKS=2` | verify-before-done | Stop blocks allowed per session |
| `FOUNDRY_VERIFY_TEST_PATTERN='^just test'` | verify-before-done | extra regex that counts as a test command |
| `FOUNDRY_VERIFY_IRREVERSIBLE_PATTERN='^make release'` | verify-before-done | extra regex that needs `VERIFY_OK=1` |
| `FOUNDRY_VERIFY_IGNORE='*.json,config/*'` | verify-before-done | extra globs that do not count as code edits |
| `FOUNDRY_WORKTREE_GUARD=0` | worktree-guard | disable |
| `FOUNDRY_WORKTREE_GUARD_WARN=1` | worktree-guard | warn instead of deny |
| `FOUNDRY_STALE_WRITE_GUARD=0` | stale-write-guard | disable |
| `FOUNDRY_STALE_WRITE_ENFORCE=0` | stale-write-guard | warn instead of deny (the warning arrives after the write, so it protects nothing) |
| `FOUNDRY_SHIP_WORKPLAN=path` | ship-stop | arm it (relative paths resolve from the project directory) |
| `FOUNDRY_SHIP_MILESTONE=M3.2` | ship-stop | the milestone to finish (default: the first open one) |
| `FOUNDRY_SHIP_MAX_BLOCKS=8` | ship-stop | continuation cap per milestone per session (above 8, Claude Code's own cap may end the turn first; see ship-stop) |
| `FOUNDRY_SHIP_STOP=0` | ship-stop | disable |
| `FOUNDRY_GUARDRAILS_STATE_DIR`, `FOUNDRY_GUARDRAILS_LOG` | all | override where state and the log go |

## How each hook behaves

### destructive-guard

Each command is normalized before matching. `sudo`, `env VAR=x`, `nohup`, `timeout`, `xargs` and leading `VAR=x` assignments are stripped. `bash -c '...'`, `sh -c`, `eval` and `$(...)` are unwrapped and checked as their own commands. Chains (`;`, `&&`, `||`, `|`) are split. Text inside a commit message or an `echo` is not a command, so `git commit -m "never rm -rf /"` is allowed.

Allowed on purpose, because blocking them would get the guard switched off: `rm -rf node_modules`, `rm -rf ./dist`, `git status`, `git push --force-with-lease` to a feature branch, `git reset --hard` on a clean tree, `DELETE FROM t WHERE ...`, `curl ... -o install.sh`.

Example deny, as Claude sees it:

```text
[foundry-guardrails/destructive-guard] Blocked destructive command (rule git-reset-hard):
git reset --hard would throw away uncommitted changes. Run git stash (recoverable) or
commit first. ...
```

SQL rules apply only when the command calls a database client (`psql`, `mysql`, `sqlite3`, `duckdb`, `supabase db`, `prisma db execute`, `wrangler d1 execute`, ...). An `echo "DROP TABLE"` is not blocked. A `WHERE` that is always true (`WHERE 1`, `WHERE 1=1`, `WHERE true`, `WHERE 'x'='x'`, `WHERE id=id`, `WHERE id=2 OR 1=1`) counts as no `WHERE`.

### secret-guard

Anything a command prints, or a file Claude reads, goes into the conversation and to the model provider. The guard denies the read or print, and points Claude at the safe forms:

| Allowed | Denied |
|---|---|
| `source .env && npm run dev` | `cat .env`, `head .env`, `grep KEY .env`, `Read(.env)` |
| `test -f .env`, `ls -la .env`, `grep -q KEY .env` | `echo $API_KEY`, `source .env && echo $DATABASE_URL` |
| `cp .env.example .env`, `cat .env.example` | `env`, `printenv`, `printenv OPENAI_API_KEY` |
| `docker run --env-file .env app` | `gh auth token`, `op read ...`, `security find-generic-password -w` |
| `cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub` | `cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519`, `git show HEAD:.env` |
| key names only: `cut -d= -f1 .env`, `sed 's/=.*//' .env`, `awk -F= '{print $1}' .env`, `grep -o '^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*' .env`, `env \| cut -d= -f1` (optionally piped into `sort`, `uniq`, `wc`, `head`, `tail`) | `cut -d= -f2 .env`, `awk -F= '{print $2}' .env`, names-only forms on a `.env` with a multi-line value or a long token in a comment (they would print part of it) |

Secret files: `.env` and `.env.*` (but not `.env.example`, `.sample`, `.template`, `.dist`), `.envrc`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, `*.p12`, SSH private keys, `~/.aws/credentials`, `.netrc`, `.npmrc`, `.pypirc`, `.git-credentials`, docker and kube configs, the GitHub CLI hosts file, gcloud credentials, `credentials.json`, `service-account*.json`, `secrets.{json,yaml,toml}`.

### verify-before-done

1. A code change marks the session "untested". The hook sees it two ways:
   - **By effect, in a git repo.** At the session's first hook call it records every dirty or untracked source file with its content hash, plus `HEAD`. At Stop (and when `VERIFY_OK=1` is used) it compares again. A source file whose content changed, including in a commit made since, is a change, whatever tool made it: `Edit`, `sed -i`, `cat > f <<EOF`, `tee`, `cp`/`mv`, a Python script, `git apply`. Source means code extensions (`.py`, `.ts`, `.go`, `.html`, `.css`, `.sql`, ... and `Makefile`, `Dockerfile`). Docs (`*.md`, `*.txt`, `*.rst`, `docs/`), data and side-effect files a program writes (`.json`, `.db`, `.log`, lockfiles), dependency and build folders, files outside the project, and files that were already dirty and that the session did not touch do not count.
   - **By tool.** Every `Edit`/`Write` to a non-doc file inside the project (in git, not once the file is back to what it was).
   - Effects cannot tell who made a change: an edit you make in your editor, or another Claude session in the same checkout, counts too. Run parallel sessions in separate worktrees.
   - **Outside git**, a command-pattern fallback: the targets of `>`/`>>`, `tee`, `sed -i`, `perl -i`, `cp`, `mv`, inline `python -`/`node -e` code that writes a file, `git apply` and `patch`. A script file that writes code (`python gen.py`) is not seen there.
2. A Bash test or typecheck marks it "tested" and moves the baseline to the code that test saw: `pytest`, `python -m unittest`, `uv run pytest`, `npm test`, `npm run test:unit`, `pnpm typecheck`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `vitest`, `jest`, `go test`, `cargo test`, `mvn test`, `gradle test`, `dotnet test`, `make test`, and more. The command has to start a stage, so `echo pytest` does not count.
3. On Stop: if code changed since the last test run, Claude gets one "keep working" message with this reason, then continues:

   ```text
   [foundry-guardrails/verify-before-done] Code changed in 2 file(s) (app.py, api.py) and no test
   or typecheck command has run since. Before finishing: run the project's tests or
   typecheck ..., and report the command and its result. If this change cannot be tested, say so
   plainly and explain why. (block 1 of at most 2 this session; FOUNDRY_VERIFY=0 disables)
   ```

   It is sent as Stop hook feedback (`hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext`, the documented non-error path), so Claude Code labels it "Stop hook feedback". Earlier versions of this plugin used `decision: "block"`, which Claude Code labels "Stop hook error occurred · ctrl+o to see". Either way it is the guard working, not a crash: press ctrl+o to read the reason, or check `guardrails.log`.
4. It cannot loop. When Claude stops again while `stop_hook_active` is true after this hook's own message, the stop is allowed, an "unverified stop" line is logged, and the baseline resets so the next turn is not nagged about the same change. When a different Stop hook (ship-stop) is what kept Claude going, the check still runs, so code written during those continuations is still checked. The session-wide cap (default 2) and Claude Code's own cap back that up. While background tasks are still running (a test run in the background, for example), the stop is allowed and the change stays pending.
5. Irreversible commands are denied until the command carries `VERIFY_OK=1`, for example `VERIFY_OK=1 git push origin feature`, and the token is refused while code changed since the last test run: "run the tests first; VERIFY_OK=1 is for after they pass". Tests in the same command count only when they gate the push: `pytest && VERIFY_OK=1 git push`. With `;`, `||`, `&` or a pipe in between (`pytest; VERIFY_OK=1 git push`, `npm test | tail && ...`) the push would run whatever the tests report, so it is refused. A command the hook denies never runs, so its tests do not count either. The token is logged. If the project has no tests, the agent is told to hand the command to you instead; `FOUNDRY_VERIFY=0` is the human override.
6. When `destructive-guard` also denies a command (a force push to `main`, for example), this hook stays silent. Claude Code passes only one deny reason to the model when two hooks deny the same call, so the more important one is the one Claude gets.

### worktree-guard

When the session's working directory is inside a linked worktree (`git worktree add`, or Claude Code's own worktrees), an edit through an absolute path into the main checkout is denied, and the reason names the same file inside your worktree. Edits inside your worktree, to `/tmp`, to another repo, or to another worktree are allowed. In the main checkout the hook does nothing.

### stale-write-guard

A `Write` replaces the whole file with what Claude holds in context. The hook protects uncommitted changes that this session did not make (yours, a formatter's, another session's). After every `Edit`/`Write`/`MultiEdit` the session makes, it records the file's content hash. A `Write` is then allowed when the file is new, untracked, outside git, clean against `HEAD`, identical to the new content, or still exactly what this session last wrote. Otherwise it is **denied**, even after a Read, and Claude is told to use `Edit` for a targeted change, or to ask you to commit or stash first. With `FOUNDRY_STALE_WRITE_ENFORCE=0` it only warns, and the warning reaches Claude after the write has already replaced the file, so warn mode does not prevent the overwrite.

### ship-stop

Keeps Claude working until a milestone in your workplan is checked off. The workplan format:

```markdown
- [x] M3.1 Schema migration
- [ ] M3.2 Export endpoint returns CSV
  - acceptance: GET /export?fmt=csv returns 200 with a header row
  - acceptance: pytest tests/test_export.py passes
- [!] M3.3 Payment webhook (blocked: needs a sandbox key from a human)
```

- `- [ ]` is open, `- [x]` is done, and `- [!]` or `- [-]` is blocked or deferred, with the reason on the same line. Only an open milestone blocks.
- Indented lines under a milestone are quoted back to Claude as its acceptance notes.
- After 8 continuations on one milestone (`FOUNDRY_SHIP_MAX_BLOCKS`), the stop is allowed and you see "a human needs to look at it" (a `systemMessage`). The default is 8 because Claude Code ends the turn itself once Stop hooks have continued it 8 times in a row with no tool call in between: it overrides the 9th block and says "A hook blocked the turn from ending 9 consecutive times" (observed on Claude Code 2.1.308). `CLAUDE_CODE_STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP` raises that limit. With a plugin cap above Claude Code's, the plugin's message may never show.
- Each continuation is sent as Stop hook feedback, not an error (see verify-before-done, point 3). Older builds showed "Stop hook error occurred" here; that was the guard working.
- A missing file, an unknown milestone id, or background tasks still running all allow the stop.

Arm it for one run:

```bash
FOUNDRY_SHIP_WORKPLAN=WORKPLAN.md FOUNDRY_SHIP_MILESTONE=M3.2 claude
```

## State and logs

Per-session markers and the log go in `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}/state/` when Claude Code provides it, and otherwise in `${TMPDIR}/foundry-guardrails/`. Every deny, warning, Stop block and unverified stop is one JSON line in `guardrails.log`:

```json
{"ts": "2026-10-28T07:40:46", "hook": "secret-guard", "action": "deny", "session": "abc123", "tool": "Bash", "reason": "Blocked: this command prints a dotenv file (.env). ...", "command": "cat .env"}
```

Read it to see what the agent tried, and to tune false positives.

## Failure behavior

Every hook **fails open**. Malformed stdin, a missing `git`, an unwritable state directory or a bug in the hook itself leads to exit 0 with no output, so the tool call goes ahead and an `error-fail-open` line is logged. A broken guard must never brick a session. The cost is that a broken guard is silent, so check the log after you change a hook.

## Tests

```bash
cd plugins/foundry-guardrails
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

145 tests. They cover the allow and deny cases for each rule, the false positives listed above, malformed stdin, the disable switches, the Stop loop caps, and real temporary git repos and worktrees. The hooks were also checked end to end in a live `claude -p --plugin-dir` session: `cat .env` was denied, and a code edit with no tests got exactly one Stop block.

## Known limitations

- Pattern matching cannot see inside script files. `python leak.py` that prints `.env`, or `psql -f drop.sql`, is not caught.
- `verify-before-done` sees that a test command *ran*, not that it *passed*. The Stop message asks Claude to report the result. Review it.
- `VERIFY_OK=1` can be typed by the agent itself. It is refused while code is untested, but a test command that ran is not a test that passed. It is an audit token, not an approval. If you need a human approval step, deny the command and have the human run it.
- `secret-guard` denies `sed -i` on `.env` (a reader command naming a secret file). Edit `.env` yourself.
- The worktree guard only sees the `Edit`/`Write`/`NotebookEdit` tools, not shell writes.
- `verify-before-done` outside git reads write targets from the command text only. Inside git, a `git pull` that changes code files mid-session also counts as a change.
- `stale-write-guard` counts the session's own `sed`/heredoc changes as "not this session's", because it records only edit-tool writes. Claude is told to use `Edit` in that case.

## Credits

These hooks are small, self-contained versions of two fuller MIT-licensed projects. Use those when you need more:

- [ethos-gate](https://github.com/jddavenportOpen/ethos-gate): irreversible-action guard, credential-scrape policy with strict and sandbox tiers, an outbound GitHub action gate with an LLM judge, and a lethal-trifecta audit.
- [claude-deploy-kit](https://github.com/jddavenportOpen/claude-deploy-kit): the destructive command rule set, policy and eval gates, and the audit trail for fleets of headless agents.

For a full team harness (agents, skills, memory, hooks) built for the AI Foundry cohort, see [agent-team-kit](https://github.com/ai-foundry-byu/agent-team-kit).

## License

MIT. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

plugins.name: foundry-qa
plugins.description: Web QA: a definition-of-done gate (deployed SHA plus a Playwright journey on desktop, phone and tablet), blast-radius regression checks, axe-core accessibility, screenshot baselines, and web-qa, persona-tester and explorer agents.
plugins.readme:
# foundry-qa

Web QA for Claude Code, in code and with example users. It gives your agent a strict
definition of done, a way to find what a change could break, accessibility and visual
regression checks, and three QA agents that drive your app in a real browser.

Part of the [AI Foundry marketplace](https://github.com/ai-foundry-byu/foundry-marketplace).

## Install

Add the marketplace (once):

```text
/plugin marketplace add ai-foundry-byu/foundry-marketplace
```

Install the plugin:

```text
/plugin install foundry-qa@ai-foundry
```

Install the browser tooling the scripts use (once per machine, inside a virtual environment):

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate
```

```bash
pip install playwright
```

```bash
python3 -m playwright install chromium
```

Optional, for Safari-engine runs:

```bash
python3 -m playwright install webkit
```

## What is in it

| Item | Type | What it does | SDLC stage | Maturity |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `done-gate` | skill | Definition-of-done gate: deployed SHA check, then a Playwright journey on each device, strict exit codes | ship / verify | proven |
| `regression-check` | skill | Stack-neutral blast-radius method: grep every consumer, judge each, behavior-test the at-risk ones | build / verify | proven |
| `a11y-check` | skill | axe-core in a real browser plus a manual WCAG 2.2 AA floor checklist | verify | proven |
| `visual-baseline` | skill | Screenshot baselines, pixel diff with threshold and tolerance, deliberate approve step | verify | proven |
| `persona-run` | skill | Runs every user story as a persona on its devices, read-only; persona checks and repeat-failure tickets (used by persona-tester) | verify / user acceptance | proven |
| `explore` | skill | Read-only same-origin crawler for console errors, broken links, 5xx, overflow and empty states (used by explorer and web-qa) | verify | proven (pattern) |
| `web-qa` | agent | Drives the app with Playwright: journeys, a11y, visual, console and network errors, mobile emulation; files findings with repro steps | verify | proven |
| `persona-tester` | agent | Tests every user story as a persona across device profiles, read-only by default; reports judged versus passed; tickets repeated failures | verify / user acceptance | proven |
| `explorer` | agent | Curious-human crawler plus a manual probe list: edge cases, empty states, Back, refresh, double submit | verify | proven (pattern) |
| `skills/done-gate/scripts/done_gate.py` | script | The gate itself (journey runner, SHA check, read-only guard) | ship / verify | proven |
| `skills/persona-run/scripts/persona_run.py` | script | Persona story runner with persona checks and ticket filing | verify | proven |
| `skills/a11y-check/scripts/a11y_check.py` | script | axe-core runner | verify | proven |
| `skills/visual-baseline/scripts/visual_baseline.py` | script | capture / compare / check / approve | verify | proven |
| `skills/explore/scripts/explore.py` | script | Same-origin read-only crawler | verify | proven (pattern) |
| `skills/done-gate/scripts/qa_yaml.py` | script | Dependency-free YAML subset parser so students do not need PyYAML | support | new |
| `skills/done-gate/scripts/qa_session.py` | script | Shared browser-session helper: the `auth` block for signed-in apps (storage state, headers, cookies, login steps), the `login` helper that saves a storage state, the settle wait, and the Playwright-missing fix | support | new |
| `skills/done-gate/templates/done-journey.yaml` | template | Annotated journey to copy into your repo | ship | new |
| `skills/persona-run/templates/stories.example.json` | template | Example of the foundry-sdlc stories.json shape, with an optional `qa` block on scripted stories | requirements / verify | new |
| `skills/persona-run/templates/personas/*.md` | template | Persona template plus two examples: first-time mobile user, power user on desktop | requirements / verify | new |

Every script lives inside the skill that uses it, so each skill folder works on its own.
`done_gate.py`, `qa_yaml.py` and `qa_session.py` are shared: the canonical copies are in `skills/done-gate/scripts/`,
and byte-identical copies sit in the other skills that import them (`explore` also carries a
copy of `persona_run.py`). `vendor.json` lists every copy and its canonical file, and
`tests/test_vendor.py` fails if a copy drifts. Edit the canonical file, then re-copy.

### What "maturity" means here

- **proven**: generalized from a tool that runs in production in our own Claude Code harness
  today. The method and the exit-code contracts come from that tool. The code in this plugin is
  a fresh, dependency-light rewrite of it for public use, tested against a fixture site in a
  real browser (see Tests below).
- **proven (pattern)**: the approach runs in production in our harness; this version's
  details (the crawl signals and probe list) were written for this marketplace.
- **new**: written for this marketplace from documentation and best practice, not yet
  battle-tested.

## How to use each item

### done-gate (skill)

Ask: "run the done gate on the signup feature" or "is this done? prove it". The skill walks
the agent through writing `qa/done-journey.yaml` and running:

```bash
python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/done-gate/scripts/done_gate.py" --journey qa/done-journey.yaml --base-url http://localhost:3000
```

Against a deployed build, with the commit check and production-safe read-only mode:

```bash
python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/done-gate/scripts/done_gate.py" --journey qa/done-journey.yaml \
  --base-url https://<your-app>.example.com \
  --sha-url https://<your-app>.example.com/api/version --sha-json-key commit --read-only
```

Exit codes: `0` pass, `1` journey fail, `2` config error, `3` SHA mismatch, `6` inconclusive.
**Only say "done" on exit 0. Inconclusive is not a pass.** Evidence goes to `.qa/done-gate/`;
after every run the gate also writes `.qa/done-gate/last.json`
(`{sha, exit, journey, devices, stories, time, failures[]}`, `sha` = the git HEAD it ran from),
which the foundry-sdlc stage detector reads. The template's `base_url: http://localhost:PORT`
takes `--port 5173` (never the PORT environment variable).

Signed-in apps: add `auth` to the journey, or pass `--storage-state`, `--header` or `--auth FILE`
to any script. Save a storage state once with the login helper:

```bash
python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/done-gate/scripts/qa_session.py" login --url http://localhost:3000/login --wait-for "[data-testid=dashboard]" --out .qa/auth.json
```

For magic-link or OAuth sign-in, add a test-only sign-in route behind an environment flag that
is never set in production, and point `auth.login_steps` at it.

Journey format (YAML subset or JSON):

```yaml
steps:
  - goto: /
  - click: "text=Get started"
  - fill: {selector: "#email", value: "qa@example.com"}
  - press: {selector: "#email", key: "Enter"}
  - wait_for: "[data-testid=dashboard]"
assertions:
  - visible: "[data-testid=dashboard]"
  - text: {selector: "h1", contains: "Welcome"}
  - url_contains: /dashboard
  - no_console_errors: true
screenshot: signup
devices: [desktop-1440x900, phone-390x844, tablet-820x1180]
stories: [US-01]                      # optional metadata: the story ids this journey covers
# auth: {storage_state: .qa/auth.json} # optional: a signed-in session
```

### regression-check (skill)

Ask: "what could this change break?" or "run a regression check before we merge". The agent
lists what changed, greps every consumer, writes a consumer table with an at-risk verdict for
each, and runs the smallest test that proves each at-risk consumer still works. This method
comes from Scott Murff's
[agent-team-kit](https://github.com/ai-foundry-byu/agent-team-kit) (`skills/regression-check`),
which is written for a SvelteKit project; this is a stack-neutral version.

### a11y-check (skill)

Ask: "check accessibility on the signup page".

```bash
python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/a11y-check/scripts/a11y_check.py" --url http://localhost:3000/signup --devices desktop-1440x900,phone-390x844
```

Exit `0` clean at `--fail-on serious`, `1` blocking violations, `2` config, `6` inconclusive.
Besides axe, the script runs its own WCAG 2.2 target-size check (2.5.8): a control under
24x24 CSS px with another target inside its 24 px circle is a blocking `target-size-2.5.8`
violation; a small but well-spaced one is listed as `small-targets` for manual review. Then the
agent walks the manual WCAG 2.2 AA checklist in the skill and reports each section as DONE,
FAILED or NOT DONE.

### visual-baseline (skill)

Ask: "check for visual regressions on home and pricing".

```bash
python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/visual-baseline/scripts/visual_baseline.py" check --url http://localhost:3000/ --name home --devices desktop-1440x900,phone-390x844
```

First run exits `6` (no baselines). Look at `.qa/visual/current/`, then `approve`. After that,
`check` exits `1` on a diff over threshold and writes red-highlight images to `.qa/visual/diff/`.
The red is a marker for changed pixels, not the page's color: compare `current/` with
`baselines/` to say what changed (`report.json` gives the `changed_box`).

### web-qa (agent)

Ask: "use web-qa to QA the checkout flow on localhost" or "QA prod after the deploy
(read-only)". It plans journeys from your acceptance criteria (or one per core flow when there
are none), runs the done gate on desktop and phone, axe, a visual check and a crawl, reads the
screenshots, re-runs failures, and always writes `.qa/findings.md` with a Repro section per
finding.

### persona-tester (agent)

Copy the persona templates into your project:

```bash
mkdir -p qa/personas && cp "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}"/skills/persona-run/templates/personas/*.md qa/personas/
```

Edit them to match your real users, then ask: "use persona-tester to test every story as the
first-time mobile user on staging". It reads the project's ONE stories.json as is (the
foundry-sdlc format, `product/stories.json`; unknown keys are warnings, never errors). A story
without a `qa` block opens `surfaces[0]` and is judged against its acceptance criteria; a
`qa: {start, steps, assertions, wait_for}` block makes it scripted. Under the hood it runs the
`persona-run` skill:

```bash
python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/persona-run/scripts/persona_run.py" --persona qa/personas/first-time-mobile-user.md --stories product/stories.json --base-url <url>
```

Checks run after the page settles (network quiet, then `qa.wait_for`, then 800 ms), and the
patience check measures navigation start to content ready. Tap targets under the persona's
minimum are reported once per device as site-wide warnings, not as story failures.

It is **read-only by default**: every POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE is answered inside the browser and
never sent, so it is safe against production. `--allow-writes` is refused for anything but
localhost. It reports `passed`, `failed`, `needs-judgment` and `inconclusive` separately, and
the agent labels its own screenshot judgments JUDGED, never passed. `--file-tickets` writes a
ticket only for failures seen on two runs in a row.

### explorer (agent)

Ask: "use explorer to find bugs on localhost:3000". It runs the read-only crawler from the `explore` skill:

```bash
python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/explore/scripts/explore.py" --url http://localhost:3000 --max-pages 30
```

It crawls hash routes (`#/group/1`) as pages and keeps each page's console and network errors
on that page. Then the agent always runs four probes on the core flow (Back after a search keeps
its state, a slow first load shows a loading indicator, the empty state has a message, double
submit), then the rest of its list (refresh mid-flow, odd input, deep links), with submit and
double-submit probes only on local or staging.

### Running the scripts without the plugin (CI)

`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` and `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}` are filled in by Claude Code inside skills
and agents. In CI or a plain terminal, copy one skill's `scripts/` folder into your repo (for
example `skills/done-gate/scripts/` to `qa/tools/`; each folder already holds every module its
script imports) and call it there:

```bash
python3 qa/tools/done_gate.py --journey qa/done-journey.yaml --base-url "$PREVIEW_URL" --read-only
```

### Install one item on its own

Every skill works copied on its own: copy `skills/<name>/` into your project's
`.claude/skills/` (or `~/.claude/skills/`). Each skill folder holds its scripts and templates,
and its SKILL.md points at them through `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}`.

| Item | On its own |
|---|---|
| `done-gate`, `a11y-check`, `visual-baseline`, `persona-run`, `explore`, `regression-check` (skills) | standalone |
| `web-qa` (agent) | needs skills `done-gate`, `a11y-check`, `visual-baseline`, `explore` (it skips a job whose skill is missing and says so) |
| `persona-tester` (agent) | needs skill `persona-run` |
| `explorer` (agent) | needs skill `explore` |
| plugin only | nothing: this plugin has no hooks, MCP server or compiled helper |

To copy an agent, put `agents/<name>.md` in `.claude/agents/` (or `~/.claude/agents/`) and the
skills it lists under `Requires skill:` in `.claude/skills/`. The agent finds them there.

## Requirements

- Python 3.9 or newer. Standard library only, except Playwright for anything that opens a browser.
- Playwright for Python and a browser build (`python3 -m playwright install chromium`).
- `a11y_check.py` downloads a pinned axe-core build from cdnjs once (cached in `.qa/cache/`),
  or uses a local file via `--axe-source`.
- Optional: Pillow speeds up decoding of very large screenshots. Not required.
- Add `.qa/` to your project's `.gitignore` (screenshots can contain real data). Commit
  `.qa/visual/baselines/` only if you want baselines in git; otherwise point `--root` elsewhere.

## Tests

From the plugin directory:

```bash
cd tests && python3 -m unittest -v
```

The unit tests (vendored copies match their canonical files, YAML parser, journey validation
including the foundry-sdlc template keys, `last.json`, SHA extraction and matching, the
exit-code contract, PNG codec, pixel diff, persona and foundry-sdlc stories.json parsing,
site-wide checks, the auth block and login-step validation, the Playwright-missing fix,
read-only rules, ticket logic, crawler URL rules for hash routes) need no browser. `test_browser_integration.py` starts a local fixture site
and runs every script in headless Chromium, including a list that loads 1.2 s after the load
event, a hash-routed page, and a page behind sign-in (headers, cookies, login steps and a saved
storage state); it skips itself if Playwright or Chromium is not installed, and the a11y cases
skip if axe-core cannot be downloaded.

Maturity note: signed-in sessions (`qa_session.py`), the 2.5.8 target-size check, hash-route
crawling and the settle wait are new in this release and so far tested only against the
fixture site.

## Known limitations

- The YAML parser is a subset: no block scalars (`|`, `>`), anchors or tags. Quote selectors.
  Use JSON if you prefer.
- `--read-only` answers blocked writes with a fake `200 {"qaReadOnly": true}`. Apps that expect
  a specific response shape may show an error state instead of success. Either way, a simulated
  write proves only that the UI responded.
- The read-only guard sees HTTP requests the page makes. It cannot stop writes sent over
  WebSockets or by a service worker that was already installed, or server-side effects of a GET.
  Never rely on it alone against a production app that changes data on GET.
- Device profiles emulate viewport, touch and user agent in Chromium. They are not real devices.
  Run `--browser webkit` for Safari-engine behavior, and test on a real phone before launch.
- Visual baselines are sensitive to OS fonts and browser version. Capture baselines and checks
  in the same environment.
- axe-core catches only part of WCAG. The manual checklist is not optional.
- The persona judgments are an agent's reading of screenshots. They are labeled JUDGED for a
  reason: they are not a substitute for watching real users.

## License

MIT. Copyright AI Foundry, BYU Marriott School of Business.

plugins.name: foundry-design
plugins.description: Design gates: a subtract-only design critic, a UI spec writer with a full state matrix and checkable acceptance criteria, a design-system template, a read-only ui-reviewer agent, and a deterministic design gate script.
plugins.readme:
# foundry-design

Design quality gates for Claude Code. Agents are good at generating screens and bad at editing
them: they ship features that pass every functional test while the experience gets worse (an
extra step, a dead button, a second panel that does the same job, gray-on-gray text). This
plugin adds the missing editor, a spec step before the build, and a scored review after it.

| Item | Type | What it does | SDLC stage | Maturity |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `design-critique` | skill | Subtract-only critic: 8-question constitution (C1-C8), findings schema, four-tier resolver, decision log | build (pre-build) and visual QA | proven |
| `ui-ux-spec` | skill | Turns a user story into a buildable UI spec: layout per breakpoint, full state matrix, keyboard and touch, copy, tokens, machine-checkable acceptance checks | design / pre-build | proven |
| `design-system` | skill | Fill-in template for your design system (tokens, contrast table, type scale, spacing, components, vocabulary) that the other items grade against | design | new |
| `ui-reviewer` | agent | Read-only REVIEW: scores screenshots plus code on a 10-dimension 0-4 rubric, returns token-level must-fixes with file:line. Never edits source | visual QA / ship | proven |
| `design_gate.py` | script (in `design-critique`, vendored into `design-system`) | Deterministic gate: clicks-to-goal, dead controls, entry points, primary buttons, tap targets, contrast, horizontal scroll, context present; fails on regression vs a baseline | visual QA / CI | new (generalized from a proven per-project gate) |
| `validate_findings.py` | script (in `design-critique`) | Validates a critique findings file: no "add" verb, deltas on flow findings, nit cap, grounding; with `--verdicts`, one C1-C8 verdict line per surface | visual QA | new |
| `design-gate.config.json`, `findings.example.json`, `decision.yaml` | templates (in `design-critique/templates/`) | Starting files for the gate config, a findings run, and a decision-log entry | setup | new |

Maturity: **proven** means generalized from a tool that runs in production in our harness today.
**new** means written for this marketplace from docs and best practice, not yet battle-tested.
`design_gate.py` is the generalized form of a gate that runs in production for one of our apps;
the generic config-driven version, the contrast and target checks, and the validator are new.

## Install

Add the marketplace:

```
/plugin marketplace add ai-foundry-byu/foundry-marketplace
```

Install the plugin:

```
/plugin install foundry-design@ai-foundry
```

Reload so the skills and agent appear (or restart Claude Code):

```
/reload-plugins
```

To try it from a local clone without installing:

```bash
claude --plugin-dir ./plugins/foundry-design
```

## How the pieces fit

```
user story -> ui-ux-spec (spec + acceptance checks)
           -> design-critique pre-build (C3/C5/C6/C8 on the plan)
           -> build
           -> design_gate.py (objective numbers, hard-fails regressions)
           -> ui-reviewer agent (scored rubric, must-fixes)
           -> design-critique post-build (subtract-only pass, decision log)
           -> ship
```

All project state lives in a `design/` directory at your repo root:

```
design/
  design-system.md        # from the design-system skill
  vocabulary.md           # one name per act
  core-flows.md           # the 1-3 jobs that matter, as steps
  design-gate.json        # gate config (copy skills/design-critique/templates/design-gate.config.json)
  design-baseline.json    # written by the gate's bless command, committed
  specs/<surface>.md      # from ui-ux-spec
  reviews/                # ui-reviewer reports and captures
  findings/               # design-critique runs (JSON arrays)
  decisions/              # one YAML per ruling
  references/             # pinned good-*.png / bad-*.png examples
```

## Install one item on its own

Every skill works when its folder is copied on its own into `.claude/skills/<name>/` or
`~/.claude/skills/<name>/`: each skill carries every file it runs or reads, referenced as
`${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/...`.

| Item | Standalone? | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| `design-critique` skill | yes | nothing (holds `design_gate.py`, `validate_findings.py`, the schema and templates) |
| `ui-ux-spec` skill | yes | nothing |
| `design-system` skill | yes | nothing (carries a vendored copy of `design_gate.py` for the contrast math) |
| `ui-reviewer` agent | yes, with skills | the `ui-ux-spec` skill (rubric, floor) and the `design-critique` skill (gate); it tells you if either is missing |

This plugin has no hooks and no plugin-only items. Vendored copies are listed in `vendor.json`
and must stay byte-identical to their canonical file.

## Using each item

### design-critique (skill, proven)

Ask: "critique the design of my app", "what can I remove from the settings page", or
`/foundry-design:design-critique`. Pre-build it critiques the plan. Post-build it runs the gate
(creating `design/design-gate.json` and the baseline on the first run when they are missing),
writes one `Cn <surface> - clean|finding` verdict line per question per surface to
`design/findings/<date>-<surface>.verdicts.md`, and writes a findings file. The critic may only
propose `remove`, `merge`, `relabel`, `inline` or `escalate`. Validate both:

```bash
python3 skills/design-critique/scripts/validate_findings.py design/findings/2026-01-15-settings.json \
  --verdicts design/findings/2026-01-15-settings.verdicts.md
```

A diff_hint that proposes an addition ("add a filter row") prints a warning; naming the app's own
control in quotes ("Delete the 'Create a group' FAB") and `escalate` findings do not.

Which to ask for: "critique / simplify / what can I remove / design pass before we ship" is this
skill; "score / rate / review the UI against a rubric / what to fix first" is the `ui-reviewer`
agent.

Inside a session the skill uses `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/...`, which Claude Code expands to
the skill's own folder. From a terminal, locate the scripts:

```bash
find "$HOME/.claude/plugins" "$HOME/.claude/skills" .claude/skills -path '*design-critique/scripts/*' -name '*.py' 2>/dev/null
```

For CI, copy `skills/design-critique/scripts/design_gate.py` and
`skills/design-critique/scripts/validate_findings.py` into your repo (MIT). Each is a single
stdlib file; `validate_findings.py` reads `../findings.schema.json` by default (pass `--schema`
to point elsewhere).

### ui-ux-spec (skill, proven)

Ask: "spec the checkout screen from story US-14" or `/foundry-design:ui-ux-spec`. It fills
`references/spec-template.md` into `design/specs/<surface>.md`, self-checks against
`references/floor-checklist.md`, and maps its acceptance checks to gate metrics.

### design-system (skill, new)

Ask: "set up our design system" or `/foundry-design:design-system`. It inventories the raw
values your code actually uses, collapses them into tokens, measures contrast for every
text/background pair, and writes `design/design-system.md` from the template. For choosing an
aesthetic direction on a greenfield product, use Anthropic's official `frontend-design` skill from
the `claude-plugins-official` marketplace; this plugin does not copy it.

### ui-reviewer (agent, proven)

Ask: "have the ui-reviewer score the dashboard against design/specs/dashboard.md". It captures
screenshots (via the gate or Playwright), reads the code, scores 10 dimensions 0-4, and returns a
verdict (`SHIP`, `SHIP AFTER MUST-FIXES`, `REWORK`, `REDESIGN`) with must-fixes that each carry
evidence, problem, a token-level fix and a verification step. The total is the plain sum of the
ten rows and the band is read off that total (a gate dimension at 0-1 or a Blocker can only lower
it). Every cited `file:line` is re-read before it is reported. It always saves the report to
`design/reviews/<date>-<surface>.md`, writes capture scripts and screenshots only under
`design/reviews/captures/`, and never edits product source. The rubric is
`skills/ui-ux-spec/references/rubric.md`.

### design_gate.py (script, new)

1. Install Playwright (only the measuring step needs it):

   ```bash
   python3 -m pip install playwright
   python3 -m playwright install chromium
   ```

2. Copy `skills/design-critique/templates/design-gate.config.json` to `design/design-gate.json` and edit `base_url`,
   `pages`, `flows` (click steps to a goal selector), `context_checks` and
   `selectors.primary_button`.
3. Start your app locally, then establish the baseline and commit it (the `design-critique` skill
   does this itself on its first run when no baseline exists):

   ```bash
   python3 path/to/design_gate.py run --config design/design-gate.json --bless
   ```

4. On every UI change:

   ```bash
   python3 path/to/design_gate.py run --config design/design-gate.json
   ```

Exit codes: 0 pass, 1 regression or hard-limit violation, 2 config error, 3 refused a
non-local `base_url` (flows can write data, so the gate only drives localhost unless you set
`"allow_remote": true` for a read-only target), 6 INCONCLUSIVE: the environment stopped the
measurement (Playwright's browser not installed or crashed, a page navigation timed out, the app
not reachable). 6 is not a pass and not a design regression; the message says what to fix, then
rerun. A click or goal that times out inside a flow is still a real result (`reached: false`).

Hard limits (fail even without a baseline, each can be set to `null` to rely on the baseline
only, which helps when adopting the gate on an existing app): one primary button per screen,
no horizontal scroll (`scrollWidth > clientWidth`, measured against the layout viewport, so it
fires on phone emulation too), zero targets under 24 px on any viewport (WCAG 2.5.8; inline links
in a sentence, hidden and off-screen elements such as a parked skip link are exempt), zero text
under 4.5:1 (3:1 large), zero unlabeled buttons, every core flow reaches its goal. Touch targets
between 24 and 44 px (`limits.min_touch_target`) are printed as `advisory (not gated)` notes and
listed under `touch_advisory` in the details; they never fail the gate. Regressions against
the baseline: any increase in clicks, dead controls, entry points or the counts above, any
context check or flow that stops holding, and any metric that disappears.

`check` and `bless` are stdlib only, so a collector in another language can write the metrics
JSON and reuse the comparison:

```bash
python3 design_gate.py check --current metrics.json --baseline design/design-baseline.json
```

Keep the gate honest: plant a known-bad on a branch (an extra click, a disabled button, a second
primary) and confirm the gate exits 1. The unit tests do exactly this.

## Tests

```bash
cd plugins/foundry-design
python3 -m unittest discover -s skills/design-critique/scripts/tests -v
```

Color math and WCAG contrast, page evaluation, hard limits, planted regressions, config
validation, the CLI, infrastructure failures as INCONCLUSIVE, the findings validator (addition
warnings, verdict coverage), and end-to-end Playwright runs against local fixture pages (phone
overflow at 390 px, off-screen skip link and inline-link exemptions, an unreachable navigation).
The end-to-end tests are skipped when Playwright or Chromium is not installed, or when the browser
crashes under machine load.

## Requirements

- Claude Code with plugin support.
- Python 3.9+ (stdlib) for the scripts.
- Playwright for Python plus a Chromium (or WebKit) build, only for `design_gate.py measure|run`
  and for the reviewer's own captures.

## Known limitations

- Contrast is computed from computed `color` and `background-color` only. Text over background
  images or gradients is counted as unknown, and element `opacity` and `mix-blend-mode` are
  ignored. Check those by eye.
- Clicks-to-goal counts the `click` steps you wrote in the config; it does not discover a shorter
  path. Keep flows written as the real user path.
- `entry_points` and `primary_buttons` depend on your selectors; a wrong selector silently counts
  0 (an invalid selector counts -1).
- The reviewer's screen-reader and latency claims are judgment, not measurement, unless you add
  tests for them; the agent labels them so.
- The design system template is a starting point, not a token pipeline: it does not generate CSS.

## License

MIT. Grounding references (WCAG, Nielsen heuristics, platform guidelines) are cited by link; no
third-party text is vendored.

plugins.name: foundry-devices
plugins.description: Native and desktop QA agents for iOS Simulator, Android, Windows and macOS, plus a device-matrix skill that runs them as parallel lanes and merges one PASS/FAIL/INCONCLUSIVE matrix.
plugins.readme:
# foundry-devices Native and device QA agents, one per platform, so you can grab the one for your target. Each agent is an operating manual that a Claude Code subagent follows: prerequisites, a doctor check it runs first, a drive loop (launch, act, screenshot, read the UI tree, assert, repeat), evidence capture to `.qa//`, and a report with PASS, FAIL or INCONCLUSIVE per user story. ## Honest status: read this first Everything in this plugin is **new**. It was written for this marketplace from official documentation (Apple simctl and System Events, Android SDK, Maestro, pywinauto, Playwright) and best practice. It is **not** generalized from a tool we run in production. **What has been run for real.** In October 2026 every script, and the exact commands from every agent's drive loop, ran on GitHub Actions runners against system apps: an Android API 34 emulator (Settings), an iOS 26.2 simulator on Xcode 16.4 (Settings), Windows Server 2025 (classic Notepad) and macOS 26 (Calculator and TextEdit). Final run: 40731526347, green on all four jobs. The screenshots show the real screens. The campaign turned up 11 defects (8 reproduced on a runner, 3 found by reading the code), all fixed in this version (see "CI-verified, and what is not" below). **What has not.** No student's agent has yet run one of these agents end to end on a real app: building it, installing it and judging real user stories. The app build paths (`xcodebuild`, XCUITest, `gradlew` + `adb install`, Electron), Appium and WinAppDriver, a USB phone, two Android devices at once, arm64 emulator images, Windows 11 Store apps and WSL interop are all untested. What we do run in production today, for comparison: - A **real iPhone** driver (iPhone Mirroring on a Mac). That one is proven and lives in its own plugin, **foundry-iphone-mirror**. Use it for stories that need real hardware. - **Playwright mobile emulation** for web apps, in the **foundry-qa** plugin. We have nothing proven for the iOS Simulator, Android native, Windows desktop or macOS desktop apps. These agents are CI-verified for the drive loops listed below, which is more than a written plan and less than a field record. **If you use one, please report back** (open an issue or a pull request on the marketplace repo) with what worked, what broke, and the exact tool versions. Two or three good field reports and we will promote an item to proven. ## Install Add the marketplace (once): ```text /plugin marketplace add ai-foundry-byu/foundry-marketplace ``` Install this plugin: ```text /plugin install foundry-devices@ai-foundry ``` From a shell instead of a session: ```bash claude plugin install foundry-devices@ai-foundry --scope project ``` ## What is inside | item | type | what it does | SDLC stage | maturity | |---|---|---|---|---| | `ios-qa` | agent | iOS Simulator QA: simctl boot/install/launch/openurl/screenshot/recordVideo/privacy/status_bar, Maestro flows, optional XCUITest | QA / verify | new (CI-verified drive loop) | | `android-qa` | agent | Android QA: AVD + emulator, adb install/am start/input/screencap, uiautomator UI tree, logcat crashes, dumpsys, Maestro, optional Appium | QA / verify | new (CI-verified drive loop) | | `windows-qa` | agent | Windows desktop QA: pywinauto UIA backend, find by automation id/name, invoke/type, control tree, screenshots, event log; Playwright for web, WinAppDriver/Appium optional | QA / verify | new (CI-verified drive loop) | | `macos-qa` | agent | macOS desktop QA: System Events accessibility tree, AXPress, keystroke, screencapture, cliclick, Playwright `_electron` for Electron apps | QA / verify | new (CI-verified drive loop) | | `device-matrix` | skill | choose device lanes from each story's `devices[]`, run them in parallel, merge one matrix and verdict | QA / plan + report | new | | `device-doctor` | skill | preflight per platform (tools present and responding, host OS, permissions), writes `.qa//doctor.json` | QA / setup | new (unit-tested, CI-run on all 4 platforms) | | `android-ui-tree` | skill | read an Android `uiautomator dump`: outline, find by text/id/desc, print a safe `adb -s shell input tap` for exactly one match | QA / drive | new (unit-tested on a real dump, CI-run) | | `macos-ax-tree` | skill | dump, outline, search and AXPress a macOS app's accessibility tree; window bounds for screenshots | QA / drive | new (parsing unit-tested, CI-run) | | `skills/device-matrix/scripts/device_matrix.py` | script | `plan`, `init`, `report` for the device matrix | QA / plan + report | new (unit-tested) | | `skills/device-doctor/scripts/doctor.py` | script | the device-doctor check runner | QA / setup | new (unit-tested) | | `skills/android-ui-tree/scripts/uitree.py` | script | the android-ui-tree helper | QA / drive | new (unit-tested) | | `skills/macos-ax-tree/scripts/ax_tree.py` | script | the macos-ax-tree helper | QA / drive | new (parsing unit-tested) | | `skills/device-matrix/templates/maestro/android-sign-in.yaml` | template | Maestro sign-in flow for Android | QA / drive | new | | `skills/device-matrix/templates/maestro/ios-sign-in.yaml` | template | Maestro sign-in flow for the iOS Simulator | QA / drive | new | | `skills/device-matrix/templates/stories.example.json` | template | stories with `devices[]` | QA / plan | new | | `skills/device-matrix/templates/results.example.json` | template | the per-lane results file every agent writes | QA / report | new | | `skills/device-matrix/templates/matrix.template.md` | template | what a finished matrix looks like | QA / report | new | Every script and template lives inside the skill that uses it, so each skill folder is complete on its own. The agents carry no files: they find their scripts in the skills they name. There are no hooks in this plugin. Nothing runs unless you ask for it. ## How to use each item ### The agents Ask for them by name or by task. Claude Code picks the agent from its description, or you can name it: ```text Use the android-qa agent to test story S1 in stories.json against app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk with the test account in QA_EMAIL / QA_PASSWORD. ``` Every agent does the same four things in order: 1. **Doctor**: its first command is the device-doctor skill's `doctor.py --platform

`, before any check of its own, and it reports READY or the exact fixes. It stops if not ready, and it never writes `doctor.json` itself. 2. **Drive loop** per story: arrange a clean state, act through the UI tree (never guessed coordinates), wait for a condition, screenshot, assert, and look at the screenshot itself. 3. **Evidence** under `.qa//`, named `--.png` plus tree dumps and logs. 4. **Report**: `.qa//results.json` plus a short table. PASS needs evidence, FAIL needs a reproduction note and logs, INCONCLUSIVE says what blocked it. All agents follow the same safety rules: test accounts and test data only, never production or a real person's account unless you say so in the task, never erase devices or simulators they did not create, secrets only through environment variables. ### The device-matrix skill ```text /foundry-devices:device-matrix ``` Or just say "run the device matrix for stories.json". The skill walks through: ```bash python3 "${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/device_matrix.py" plan stories.json python3 "${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/device_matrix.py" init stories.json --qa .qa # ... one subagent per lane, in parallel ... python3 "${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/device_matrix.py" report stories.json --qa .qa # exit 0 PASS, 1 FAIL, 3 INCONCLUSIVE ``` ### The scripts on their own All scripts are Python 3 standard library only and print `--help`. From the plugin folder: ```bash python3 skills/device-doctor/scripts/doctor.py --platform android python3 skills/android-ui-tree/scripts/uitree.py tap .qa/android/ui.xml --text "Sign in" --exact --clickable --serial emulator-5554 python3 skills/macos-ax-tree/scripts/ax_tree.py dump "Calculator" --depth 8 --out .qa/macos/ax.json python3 skills/macos-ax-tree/scripts/ax_tree.py find .qa/macos/ax.json --role AXButton --id Seven python3 skills/macos-ax-tree/scripts/ax_tree.py press "Calculator" ``` Current Calculator keys have an identifier (`Seven`, `Equals`) and no name, so search them with `--id`. Use the path `find` prints: it changes between macOS versions. ### Install one item on its own You can copy a single skill or agent instead of installing the whole plugin. - **Skills, standalone:** `device-matrix`, `device-doctor`, `android-ui-tree`, `macos-ax-tree`. Copy the whole skill folder (for example `skills/device-doctor/`) to `.claude/skills/` in your project or to `~/.claude/skills/`. Each folder holds every script and template it uses. - **Agents, need skills:** copy the agent file to `.claude/agents/` or `~/.claude/agents/` and copy the skills it names on its `Requires skill:` line: - `ios-qa`: `device-doctor`, `device-matrix` (Maestro templates) - `android-qa`: `device-doctor`, `android-ui-tree`, `device-matrix` (Maestro templates) - `macos-qa`: `device-doctor`, `macos-ax-tree` - `windows-qa`: `device-doctor` - **Plugin only:** nothing. This plugin has no hooks, MCP servers or compiled helpers.
