The `device-matrix` skill hands lanes to the four agents (and to the foundry-qa and foundry-iphone-mirror plugins), so install those for a full multi-device run. ## Requirements | lane | host | install | |---|---|---| | ios-qa | macOS | Xcode (open it once, accept the license, install an iOS runtime); Maestro: `curl -fsSL "https://get.maestro.mobile.dev" \| bash`, then `export PATH="$PATH:$HOME/.maestro/bin"` in the same shell (the installer only edits rc files) and `maestro --version`; a JDK 17+ for Maestro | | android-qa | macOS, Linux or Windows | Android SDK platform-tools, emulator, cmdline-tools (via Android Studio or `sdkmanager`); Maestro optional (same install and `export PATH` as ios-qa); Appium optional (`npm i -g appium`, `appium driver install uiautomator2`) | | windows-qa | native Windows 10/11 (not WSL) | Python 3, `py -m pip install pywinauto pillow`; Playwright optional for web | | macos-qa | macOS | Accessibility and Screen Recording permission for the app running Claude Code (the doctor probes Accessibility; it cannot probe Screen Recording and shows that row as `??`, unknown); `brew install cliclick` optional; Node + `npm i -D playwright` for Electron apps | | device-matrix | any | Python 3 | ## Tests ```bash cd plugins/foundry-devices python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v ``` The tests cover the logic in the scripts (UI tree parsing and matching, the clickable-row resolution and the tap serial on a trimmed real API 34 Settings dump, the tap ambiguity guard, the accessibility tree on a trimmed real macOS 26 Calculator dump, matrix planning and verdict rules, doctor timeouts, adb parsing, the Maestro fix line and the unprobed Screen Recording row). They do not start a simulator, emulator or desktop app; the CI run below did. ## CI-verified, and what is not The device smoke workflow (`.github/workflows/device-smoke.yml` on the `test/device-smoke` branch of the marketplace repo, helpers in `.github/device-smoke/`) runs the plugin's scripts and the agents' commands verbatim on real runners. Run 40731526347 and the code review around it found these, all fixed here: | # | where | what was wrong | fix | |---|---|---|---| | D1 | ios-qa, android-qa, doctor.py | Maestro was not on `PATH` after the install line, in the same shell | `export PATH="$PATH:$HOME/.maestro/bin"` and `maestro --version` after the install, in the agents and the doctor's fix line | | D2 | uitree.py | `--clickable` found 0 matches on list rows, the skill's own headline example | a text match resolves to its nearest clickable ancestor (the row) and taps its bounds; tested on the real dump | | D3 | windows-qa | `window_text()` on an Edit returns its name ("Text Editor"), not its text | read Edit contents with `get_value()` | | D4 | ios-qa | `recordVideo` + `kill -INT` hung forever when SIGINT came before "Recording started" (53 min in CI) | wait for "Recording started", bounded stop, `kill -9` fallback | | D5 | all four agents | a plain-language session skipped the doctor and hand-wrote `doctor.json` | numbered MUST rules at the top: doctor first, stop on NOT READY, never write `doctor.json` | | D6 | windows-qa | the PowerShell lookup failed when `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` was only an environment variable | the lookup tries `$env:CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` too | | D7 | ax_tree.py, macos-qa | the `--name "7"` example does not match current Calculator | examples use `--id Seven`; `find` suggests `--id` when `--name` misses | | D8 | windows-qa | Get-WinEvent printed an error on a clean log | `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue`, prints "no matching events" | | D9 | doctor.py | the unprobed Screen Recording row printed `OK` | it prints `??` (unknown) and is never `ok` | | D10 | uitree.py | the printed tap had no `-s ` | `--serial`, `$ANDROID_SERIAL` or the only attached device; refuses when several are attached | | D11 | android-qa | the emulator boot loop ran `adb` without `-s` and could spin forever | the serial is fixed by `-port` up front, every command takes `-s`, the boot wait is bounded | Verified in CI with the corrected form: D1, D3, D4, D6, D7, D8 (the `SilentlyContinue` call). D2 was checked against the real dump that CI captured. Fixed but not yet re-run on a runner: the D2/D10 script changes as shipped (unit-tested on the real dump), the D11 boot block (`-port`, bounded wait), the D8 "no matching events" branch, and the D5 rules, which need a fresh plain-language agent session to confirm they hold. ## Known limitations - The drive loops are CI-verified against system apps only. None has been run end to end by a student's agent on a real project yet. Expect some commands to need adjusting for your tool versions. Each agent tells you to check the tool's own `--help` and to note differences in its report. - `xcrun simctl` subcommand options (for example `privacy` service names) change between Xcode releases. - `ax_tree.py dump` can be slow on large windows and needs the Accessibility permission; paths go stale as soon as the UI changes. - Windows automation needs an active, unlocked desktop session, cannot cross the UAC secure desktop, and cannot drive an elevated app from a non-elevated script. - Apps that draw their own UI (games, some cross-platform toolkits) expose little to any accessibility tree, so agents fall back to screenshots and coordinates with lower confidence. ## License MIT.

plugins.name: foundry-iphone-mirror
plugins.description: Drive a real iPhone from a Mac through macOS iPhone Mirroring: screenshot, read, tap, type, swipe, verify. A skill, an iphone-driver agent, an MCP server and a CLI with a doctor.
plugins.readme:
# foundry-iphone-mirror

Drive a real iPhone from your Mac with Claude Code. The plugin uses macOS **iPhone
Mirroring**: it screenshots the mirrored phone, lets the model read the screenshot,
injects one tap, swipe or keystroke, and screenshots again to verify. Use it for
real-device QA of your iOS app and for any on-phone task that has no Mac-side API.

**Status: proven engine, port not yet device-tested.** The engine runs in production in
our own harness today, driving a real iPhone. This marketplace port of it has passed its
unit tests but has not yet been run on a real device. Expect rough edges on first setup,
and please report what broke.

It is the only real-device iOS path in this marketplace. It does not use the iOS
Simulator, XCUITest or Appium, and it does not need a developer account or a cable.

## What's inside

| Item | Type | What it gives you | Maturity |
|---|---|---|---|
| `iphone-mirror` | skill | the screenshot, read, act, verify loop, command reference, recipes, rules | new (port of a proven engine; not yet run on a device) |
| `iphone-driver` | agent | delegate a whole on-phone task; screenshots stay in its context, you get the outcome | new (port of a proven engine; not yet run on a device) |
| `iphone-mirror` | script (CLI, on PATH) | `doctor`, `build`, `open`, `shot`, `tap`, `swipe`, `type`, `key`, `home`, `info`, `tapxy`, `map` | new (port of a proven engine; not yet run on a device) |
| `engine/worker.sh` + `engine/launcher.c` | script | the privileged worker and the Mach-O launcher sealed inside the helper app | new (port of a proven engine; not yet run on a device) |
| `engine/build-helper-app.sh` | script | builds, ad hoc signs and registers the helper app | new (port of a proven engine; not yet run on a device) |
| `iphone` | MCP server (`mcp/server.py`) | typed `iphone_*` tools; `iphone_screenshot` returns the PNG inline | new (rewrite; not yet run on a device) |

**What the labels mean.** "new" means written or changed for this marketplace and not
yet run on a real device. Every item here is new for now. The CLI, worker, launcher,
build script, skill and agent are a port of a tool that runs in production in our own
harness today, driving a real iPhone; the port changed that engine in small ways
(listed under "Changes from the source" below) that are unit-tested but not yet run on
a device. The MCP server is a rewrite: our production server uses the `mcp` Python
package, and this one is standard-library only so you install nothing. Its tool surface
is the same and it is covered by protocol tests. The labels move to "proven" once a
device run passes the acceptance check in the skill.

## Install one item on its own

Nothing in this plugin works when copied on its own. Install the whole plugin.

| Item | Standalone? | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `iphone-mirror` skill | plugin only | needs the `iphone-mirror` CLI on PATH (bin/), the `iphone` MCP server, and the helper app compiled from engine/ |
| `iphone-driver` agent | plugin only | calls the same CLI and helper app |
| `iphone` MCP server | plugin only | registered by the plugin's `.mcp.json` via `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` |

## Requirements

- macOS 15 (Sequoia) or newer, with the **iPhone Mirroring** app. Not offered in every
  region (it has been unavailable in the EU).
- An iPhone on iOS 18 or newer, signed in to the same Apple Account as the Mac, nearby,
  with Wi-Fi and Bluetooth on. Pair it once by opening iPhone Mirroring and following
  the prompts.
- Xcode Command Line Tools for `clang` (one-time, to build the helper app):
  `xcode-select --install`
- `cliclick` for clicks and keystrokes: `brew install cliclick`
- Python 3 (any 3.8+) for the MCP server. Standard library only.

## Install

Add the marketplace:

```text
/plugin marketplace add ai-foundry-byu/foundry-marketplace
```

Install the plugin:

```text
/plugin install foundry-iphone-mirror@ai-foundry
```

Then restart Claude Code so the skill, agent, CLI and MCP server load.

From a shell instead:

```bash
claude plugin install foundry-iphone-mirror@ai-foundry
```

## One-time setup (about 5 minutes)

**1. Install the tools.**

```bash
xcode-select --install
brew install cliclick
```

**2. Build the helper app.** This compiles a tiny launcher, copies the worker into an
app bundle, signs it ad hoc and registers it. Default location
`$HOME/Applications/FoundryPhone.app`.

```bash
iphone-mirror build
```

Options: `--app PATH` (must end in `.app`), `--bundle-id ID`, `--name NAME`. The chosen
path is remembered in `$HOME/Library/Application Support/foundry-iphone-mirror/helper-path`,
so the CLI and the MCP server find it without environment variables.

If `iphone-mirror` is not on your PATH (for example in a plain terminal outside Claude
Code), run it by full path from the plugin directory, `<plugin-dir>/bin/iphone-mirror`.
`claude plugin details foundry-iphone-mirror` shows where the plugin is installed.

**3. Open iPhone Mirroring and connect the phone.**

```bash
iphone-mirror open
```

Unlock or approve on the phone if asked. Keep the Mirroring window on screen (it can
be behind other windows; the CLI raises it before each capture and tap).

**4. Grant the helper app three permissions.** Only you can do this. In System Settings >
Privacy & Security:

- **Accessibility** > [+] > press Cmd-Shift-G > paste `~/Applications/FoundryPhone.app` >
  Open > switch it on.
- **Screen Recording** (called "Screen & System Audio Recording" on newer macOS) > [+] >
  same path > switch it on.

- **Automation**: the first `iphone-mirror doctor` run shows a prompt that the helper app
  "wants to control System Events" (that is how it reads the Mirroring window's position).
  Click **Allow**. If you missed it, find the helper app under Automation and switch on
  System Events. Unanswered, the doctor reports a System Events timeout after 8 seconds.

Grants take effect immediately. No restart.

**5. Run the doctor until it is clean.**

```bash
iphone-mirror doctor
```

Expected ending: `=== 9 ok, 0 fail, 0 warn ===`. Each `[FAIL]` line names its fix.

### Why a helper app?

macOS attaches Accessibility, Screen Recording and Automation grants to the *responsible process*.
Grant your terminal and only that terminal works; a headless agent process may have no
way to answer the prompt at all. The client launches the helper app through
LaunchServices once per action, so the helper is always its own responsible process
and carries its own grant, whoever calls it: a terminal, VS Code, Claude Code running
headless, or the MCP server.

The helper lives outside the plugin on purpose. The plugin directory changes on every
plugin update, and a moved bundle loses its grant.

### Security model

- The worker script is copied into the bundle and covered by the code signature.
  `doctor` runs `codesign --verify --deep --strict` on the helper and fails if anything
  edited the bundle since you built it.
- Every rebuild re-signs the app, so macOS treats it as new and asks you to approve
  the grants again. That is by design: the code holding the grant is code you rebuilt.
- Inside the bundle the worker ignores all `IPHONE_MIRROR_*` test hooks, and it parses
  its geometry cache as integers instead of sourcing it, so environment variables and
  files in the state folder cannot change what the granted app runs.
- Limit: macOS does not re-check the bundle's resources on every launch, so a process
  running as you could still edit the bundle itself. `doctor` catches that through the
  signature check; run it at the start of every session (the skill and agent do).
- To remove everything: delete the helper app, remove it from the Privacy lists
  (`tccutil reset All local.foundry.iphone-mirror` does all three for the default bundle ID), and
  delete `$HOME/Library/Caches/foundry-iphone-mirror` and
  `$HOME/Library/Application Support/foundry-iphone-mirror`.

## How to use it

### The loop: screenshot, read, act, verify

```bash
iphone-mirror shot /tmp/iphone-shots/01.png    # prints: path WxHpx window WxHpt
# Read the PNG, pick a target by its pixel position (top-left origin)
iphone-mirror tap 326 700                      # pixels from THAT screenshot
iphone-mirror shot /tmp/iphone-shots/02.png    # verify the screen changed
```

The client converts screenshot pixels to screen points using the geometry recorded by
the last `shot` (Retina 2x handled). Never send two actions without a screenshot
between them: iOS animates and scrolls, so stale coordinates miss. `iphone-mirror map
<px> <py>` prints where a tap would land without touching the phone.

### From Claude Code

- **Ask in plain words** ("open Settings on my iPhone and turn on Dark Mode", or "is my
  setup ready to test on my real iPhone?"). The `iphone-mirror` skill is meant to load
  on these phrasings, but the model may call the `iphone_*` MCP tools directly instead,
  so those tool descriptions carry the same core rules: run `iphone_doctor` first, stop
  on any FAIL, and act on the phone only for a task you asked for. If you want the full
  loop for sure, say "use the iphone-mirror skill".
- **Delegate long tasks** to the subagent: "Use the iphone-driver agent to walk
  through sign-up in my TestFlight build and screenshot each step." You get back an
  outcome, a step list and evidence paths, not 40 screenshots.
- **MCP tools** are available as `mcp__plugin_foundry-iphone-mirror_iphone__iphone_screenshot`,
  `..._iphone_tap`, `..._iphone_swipe`, `..._iphone_type`, `..._iphone_key`,
  `..._iphone_home`, `..._iphone_doctor`, `..._iphone_open`, `..._iphone_info`,
  `..._iphone_tapxy`. The screenshot comes back inline as an image.

### Real-device QA example

Write acceptance checks first, then run one loop per check and keep a screenshot as
evidence:

```text
Use the iphone-driver agent. App: <your-app> (installed from TestFlight).
Checks:
1. Launch shows the welcome screen with a "Get started" button.
2. Sign up with test account test-user-01 reaches the Home tab.
3. Home tab shows "Hi, test-user-01".
Save one screenshot per check as /tmp/iphone-shots/qa-<n>.png and report pass/fail per check.
```

## Limits

- **iPhone Mirroring must be open, connected and showing the phone.** If the phone is
  unlocked and in use, Mirroring shows "iPhone in Use" and cannot drive it: lock the
  phone. If the session drops, a human may need to approve on the device again.
- **Coordinate taps from screenshots, not element selectors.** There is no
  accessibility tree of the iOS app. Accuracy depends on the model reading the
  screenshot; small or crowded targets can miss, which is why every action is verified.
- **One phone, one action at a time.** Mirroring connects one iPhone to one Mac. The
  client holds a lock, so parallel callers queue.
- **The Mac session must be logged in and unlocked.** A Mac with no display attached
  may capture nothing; use a display or a dummy HDMI plug.
- **Some phone features do not mirror.** The camera, and some protected or
  DRM screens, appear blank or are blocked. Face ID prompts must be answered on the
  phone.
- **Gestures are basic.** Tap, drag-swipe and the home swipe. No multi-touch (pinch,
  rotate), no long-press primitive, no hardware buttons.
- **Typing sends literal keystrokes** that show on the mirror. Do not type secrets.
- **Rebuilding the helper app resets its grants.** After a plugin update, `doctor`
  warns if your helper was built from an older worker; rebuild and re-approve when
  convenient.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| `helper app missing` | `iphone-mirror build` |
| `is not running` | `iphone-mirror open`, then approve on the phone |
| `has no window` | the Mirroring window is closed or minimized; bring it back on screen |
| `window geometry unreadable` / Accessibility FAIL | add the helper app (not your terminal) under Accessibility |
| `System Events did not answer in 8s` | allow the helper app to control System Events (the prompt, or Privacy & Security > Automation) |
| `screenshot empty` / Screen Recording FAIL | add the helper app under Screen Recording |
| `cliclick not found` | `brew install cliclick`, then `iphone-mirror build` and re-approve |
| `no screenshot recorded since the last geometry read` | run `shot` before `tap` or `swipe` (`info` resets the mapping) |
| taps land in the wrong spot | the window moved or resized: take a fresh `shot` |
| LaunchServices error -10669 | the bundle is damaged: `iphone-mirror build` |
| `worker timeout` | the helper did not finish in 30s; check `doctor`, or raise `IPHONE_MIRROR_TIMEOUT` |

## Files

```
foundry-iphone-mirror/
  .claude-plugin/plugin.json
  .mcp.json                     registers the "iphone" MCP server via ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}
  bin/iphone-mirror             the CLI (added to PATH while the plugin is enabled)
  engine/worker.sh              privileged worker, copied into the helper app
  engine/launcher.c             helper app main executable (execs worker.sh)
  engine/build-helper-app.sh    build + sign + register the helper app
  mcp/server.py                 stdlib MCP server over the CLI
  skills/iphone-mirror/SKILL.md the loop and rules
  agents/iphone-driver.md       the delegation subagent
  tests/                        unit tests (no phone needed)
```

State lives in `$HOME/Library/Caches/foundry-iphone-mirror` (geometry cache, IPC
files, default screenshots). It is fixed on purpose: LaunchServices does not pass
environment variables to the helper app, so the client, the MCP server and the helper
all derive it from `$HOME`. `IPHONE_MIRROR_STATE` is honored only by the unit tests,
which run the worker in-process.

## Tests

No phone, window or permission is needed: geometry is faked and `cliclick` is replaced
by a recorder. Inside the test files, the worker is run directly instead of through the
helper app.

```bash
cd <plugin-dir> && python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

Covers pixel-to-point math (including Retina 2x and bounds), worker guards, the
geom-cache injection guard, test hooks being ignored inside a bundle, client argument
validation and locking, no `open -a "iPhone Mirroring"` when the helper app is missing
(a stub `open` on PATH), the fixed state dir, the doctor naming all three grants,
the safety rules in the MCP tool descriptions, the launcher (compiled with clang, skipped without it), and the
MCP protocol (initialize, tools/list, tools/call, inline PNG, errors).

## Changes from the source

Ported from our production plugin. What changed and why:

- Absolute paths, a personal helper app name and a personal bundle ID were replaced by
  `$HOME` defaults plus `--app`, `--bundle-id` and `--name` build options.
- State moved from a shared `/tmp` folder to a per-user `~/Library/Caches` folder.
- The worker now parses its geometry cache instead of `source`-ing it, ignores test
  hooks inside the bundle, validates coordinates and bounds, and no longer echoes typed
  text back. A helper-function bug that could swallow error messages was fixed.
- The client adds a lock (one action at a time), a `map` dry-run, and a `build` command.
  It checks that the helper app exists before raising iPhone Mirroring, so a call that
  is bound to fail never switches your screen to the phone, and `info` no longer raises
  the window at all.
  `doctor` adds macOS version, signature and version-drift checks.
- `cliclick`'s location is recorded at build time, since apps launched by LaunchServices
  get a minimal PATH.
- The MCP server was rewritten on the standard library (no `mcp` package needed).
- The System Events call that reads the window is now bounded (8 seconds), and the
  Automation grant it needs is documented. The source relied on a one-time prompt that
  could leave a fresh install hanging with no explanation.

## License

MIT. Part of the [AI Foundry marketplace](https://github.com/ai-foundry-byu/foundry-marketplace).

plugins.name: foundry-evals
plugins.description: Measure agents and prompts: scaffold an eval suite with oracles, code graders, a binary judge and negative controls, run and compare it, and hill-climb one change at a time. Ships evalkit.py (stdlib only).
plugins.readme:
# foundry-evals

Measure agents and prompts. Build an eval suite that can actually fail, run it, compare
with the last run without fooling yourself, and improve a prompt one change at a time.

Ships three skills, one auditing agent, and `evalkit.py`: a single-file, standard-library-only
Python runner you can also copy into any repo for CI.

## Install

Add the marketplace (once):

```text
/plugin marketplace add ai-foundry-byu/foundry-marketplace
```

Install the plugin:

```text
/plugin install foundry-evals@ai-foundry
```

Or from a shell:

```bash
claude plugin install foundry-evals@ai-foundry
```

## What is in it

| item | type | what it does | SDLC stage | maturity |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `new-eval` | skill | scaffold a suite: cases, target runner, code graders first, a binary judge only where code cannot grade, do-nothing and pushover controls, a threshold | test design | method proven; tooling new |
| `run-eval` | skill | run, read the report in the right order, compare with the last run, report only measured numbers | test / verify | method proven; tooling new |
| `hillclimb` | skill | one change per round, keep only changes above the noise band, train/val/test discipline, cost staircase | improve / optimize | method proven; tooling new |
| `eval-auditor` | agent | audits a suite for ambiguous cases, cheatable or over-strict graders, missing hold cases, bad judge rubrics, saturated or noisy runs | review | new |
| `skills/new-eval/scripts/evalkit.py` (also `bin/evalkit`) | script | the runner: init, run, check, compare, history; vendored into `run-eval` and `hillclimb` | test / CI gate | new (standalone port) |
| `skills/new-eval/scripts/judge_claude.py` | script | binary LLM judge through `claude -p`: critique, then a single VERDICT line | test | new |
| `skills/new-eval/templates/example-suite` | template | `refund-triage`, a 9-case suite with an offline target, a model target, controls and a deliberate bug to find | learning | new |

**Maturity, honestly.** "Proven" here means the METHOD (code graders first, binary judges,
negative controls, errors never scored as zeros, pass^k, same cases or no comparison, one
change per climb round, train/val/test splits) is how the AI Foundry team's own eval
framework works in production today. `evalkit.py`, the judge script, the agent and the
templates are NEW: a standalone port written for this marketplace, covered by unit tests but
not yet battle-tested by other teams. Report bugs as issues.

## Quickstart (2 minutes, no API key)

```bash
evalkit init evals/refund-triage
cd evals/refund-triage
evalkit check . --no-judge
evalkit run . --no-judge --gate
```

If `evalkit` is not on PATH (the plugin's `bin/` is added only while the plugin is enabled),
run `python3 skills/new-eval/scripts/evalkit.py` from the plugin folder, or copy that one file
into your repo and run `python3 evalkit.py`.

## Install one item on its own

Every skill is self-contained: copy its folder to `.claude/skills/<name>/` or
`~/.claude/skills/<name>/` and it runs its own `scripts/evalkit.py` through
`${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}`.

| item | on its own | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `new-eval` | standalone | carries the canonical `evalkit.py`, `judge_claude.py` and the example suite, so `init` works |
| `run-eval` | standalone | carries a vendored `evalkit.py` (run, check, compare, history); `init` needs `new-eval` |
| `hillclimb` | standalone | carries a vendored `evalkit.py`; scaffold with `new-eval` first |
| `eval-auditor` | needs skill `run-eval` | copy `agents/eval-auditor.md` to `.claude/agents/` and `run-eval` to `.claude/skills/run-eval/`; the agent finds it and says so if it is missing |
| `bin/evalkit` | plugin only | the PATH wrapper exists only while the plugin is enabled |

Vendored copies are listed in `vendor.json` (copy path: canonical path) and must stay
byte-identical; `tests/test_evalkit.py` checks it. Edit the canonical file, then copy it over.

The first run scores 77.8% and fails the 90% gate: two final-sale cases sit at 0% because the
example target has a deliberate bug. Ask Claude "use the hillclimb skill on this suite" to
find and fix it, then rerun and read the comparison.

## How to use each item

**new-eval.** Say "add an eval for my summarizer" or "build evals for this agent". The skill
walks through: define good, scaffold with `evalkit init`, wire your target (JSON in on stdin,
one JSON object out on stdout), write cases with oracles, choose graders, add a judge only for
fuzzy criteria, add controls, set the threshold, and pass `evalkit check`.

**run-eval.** Say "run the evals" or "did my change help". It runs a pilot, the full run with
reps, reads the report (warnings, 0% cases, failures, flips, then numbers), and reads the
comparison (NOT COMPARABLE, within noise, improved, regressed).

**hillclimb.** Say "improve this prompt against the eval" or "make it cheaper without losing
quality". One change per round, keep or revert on val, confirm on test, log every round.

**eval-auditor.** Say "audit my eval suite at evals/x". It runs the free `evalkit check`,
reads every case and the latest run, and reports findings with evidence and fixes. It does not
edit files and does not run paid model calls unless you ask.

## evalkit reference

```bash
evalkit init <dir>                       # copy the example suite (plus judge.py)
evalkit check <suite> [--no-judge]       # oracles pass, empty output fails, controls score low
evalkit run <suite> [--reps N] [--split train|val|test|all] [--cases a,b] [--tag t]
                    [--label L] [--no-judge] [--target CMD] [--out DIR]
                    [--gate | --fail-under X] [--fail-metric score|pass_hat_k]
evalkit compare <suite> | <a.json> <b.json>
evalkit history <suite>
```

Target protocol: stdin `{"case_id", "rep", "input"}`; stdout one JSON object; optional
`"_meta": {"cost_usd": n}`. Non-zero exit, timeout or non-JSON output is an error trial, kept
out of the score and listed in the report.

Graders: `exact`, `contains`, `regex`, `json_field` (`equals`, `one_of`, `exists`, `is`),
`judge`. All take `path` (dotted) and `negate`.

Judge protocol: stdin `{"case_id", "input", "expected", "output", "criterion", "rubric"}`;
stdout `{"pass": true|false|null, "reason": "..."}`. `null` (UNKNOWN) is an error, not a pass.

Outputs: `<root>/<suite>/<run_id>.json` (every trial and grader verdict, fingerprints of the
case set, graders, target command and surfaces) and `<root>/<suite>/<run_id>.md` (summary,
comparison, failures, errors).

Results root: `--out DIR` if given; otherwise `.evals` in the project root, the nearest folder
above the suite that has a `.git` (else the suite's parent folder). It never depends on the
directory you run from, so every run of a suite lands in one history and compares with the
last one. `run` prints the absolute report path; `history` prints the folder first. If an older
version left runs in `./.evals`, evalkit prints a `note:` pointing at them.

`suite.json` `target` (and `judge`) is an object `{"command": ..., "timeout_s": n}`, or a bare
command string or list as shorthand (`"target": "python3 run.py"`).

Exit codes: 0 ok, 2 config error, 3 no scorable trial, 4 below gate, 5 check failed.

CI example (GitHub Actions step):

```yaml
- run: python3 tools/evalkit.py run evals/refund-triage --gate --quiet
```

## Requirements

- Python 3.9 or newer. No packages.
- Claude Code CLI on PATH only for `judge_claude.py` and the example `target_claude.py`
  (both call `claude -p --output-format json`). Set `EVALKIT_JUDGE_MODEL` and
  `EVALKIT_TARGET_MODEL` to pin models, `EVALKIT_CLAUDE_BIN` to use another binary.

## Tests

```bash
cd plugins/foundry-evals
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

32 offline tests: every grader, pass@k and pass^k math, error handling (crash, junk stdout,
timeout), judge wiring and cost sums, the example suite end to end (baseline fails the gate,
the one-line fix passes, comparison names the two fixed cases), case-set change detection,
control and empty-output self-tests, CLI exit codes, one results history when the suite is
run from two different directories (and `--out` still overriding it), a string `target`, vendored copies byte-identical to
canonical, and a clear error when `init` runs without the example suite.

## Known limitations

- Trials run one at a time. Large suites against slow models take a while; that is deliberate.
- `claude -p` targets and judges inherit your Claude Code settings, plugins and project
  instructions from the directory they run in. For a clean measurement, run the suite from a
  directory without a project CLAUDE.md, or use your own API-based target.
- No automated hill-climber: the `hillclimb` skill drives the loop by hand with evalkit.
- No multi-turn conversation or tool-sandbox harness. For a full agent environment (mock
  store, tool-call graders, judge validation with human labels), see
  [agent-evals-starter](https://github.com/jddavenportOpen/agent-evals-starter) (MIT), which
  this plugin's control and grader ideas are adapted from.
- Bootstrap intervals over a few dozen cases are wide and somewhat optimistic (reps of one
  case are not independent). Treat small deltas as noise.

## License

MIT. Part of the [AI Foundry marketplace](https://github.com/ai-foundry-byu/foundry-marketplace).

plugins.name: foundry-builder-kit
plugins.description: Day-one build skills: add auth, a 10k-user launch audit, secrets hygiene with a commit guard, cheap structured LLM routing, scheduled headless agents, and driving interactive CLIs through tmux.
plugins.readme:
# foundry-builder-kit

Day-one build skills for student projects. Install it before you write your first route: it adds sign-in, gets the app ready for real users, keeps your API keys out of git, cuts your LLM bill on simple calls, runs agents on a schedule without silent failures, and lets an agent drive interactive terminals.

Part of the AI Foundry (BYU Marriott) marketplace.

## Install

Add the marketplace (once):

```text
/plugin marketplace add ai-foundry-byu/foundry-marketplace
```

Install the plugin:

```text
/plugin install foundry-builder-kit@ai-foundry
```

From a shell instead of a session:

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add ai-foundry-byu/foundry-marketplace
```

```bash
claude plugin install foundry-builder-kit@ai-foundry
```

Not using plugins? See "Install one item on its own" below. Every script runs on its own with `python3`.

## What is inside

| Item | Type | What it does | SDLC stage | Maturity |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `add-auth` | skill | Audits the project, recommends an auth provider with the trade-off, implements sign-in, verifies with a build and a protected-route check | build | proven |
| `scale-10k` | skill | Launch-readiness audit (the app's own state and load, auth cost, DB pooling, sessions, rate limits, email, compliance, monitoring) with a scorecard, cost table and ordered fixes | ship | proven |
| `secrets-hygiene` | skill | `.env` patterns, gitignore, gitleaks pre-commit and CI, and the probe-first rotation flow for a leaked key | build / operate | proven (rotation flow); new (templates) |
| `cheap-llm-routing` | skill | Route schema-pinned extraction or classification to a free or cheap model, with a privacy bar and a paid fallback | build | proven |
| `scheduled-agents` | skill | Headless `claude -p` on cron, launchd, Task Scheduler or GitHub Actions, with locks, timeouts, success-only heartbeats and a deadman | operate | proven (cron/launchd, deadman); new (Windows, GitHub Actions) |
| `tmux-agents` | skill | Drive REPLs, dev servers, installers and parallel coding agents through tmux on a private, per-project socket | build / test | proven |
| commit secret guard | hook | `skills/secrets-hygiene/scripts/commit_secret_guard.py`, wired in `hooks/hooks.json`. Blocks a `git commit` the agent runs when the commit would contain a secret: the index plus whatever the same command stages first (`git add -A && git commit`, `git commit -am`) | build | new |
| `skills/secrets-hygiene/scripts/scan_secrets.py` | script | Stdlib secret scanner: `--staged`, `--worktree`, `--all` (tracked plus untracked, not gitignored), or paths; redacted output | build | new |
| `skills/secrets-hygiene/scripts/probe_key.py` | script | Asks a provider whether a key still authenticates: LIVE, DEAD or ERR (ERR is never an all-clear) | operate | new |
| `skills/cheap-llm-routing/scripts/structured_router.py` | script | Forced-tool-call structured extraction across a privacy-aware provider chain with schema validation; `--mock-response` runs the whole path offline with no keys | build | new |
| `skills/scheduled-agents/scripts/run_headless.py` | script | Runs one `claude -p` job with a lock, timeout, saved transcript and success-only heartbeat | operate | new |
| `skills/scheduled-agents/scripts/deadman.py` | script | Writes heartbeats and alerts (webhook, webhook file, or command) when the last success is too old; exits 3 when the alert was not delivered or no channel is set, and leaves an alert file next to the heartbeat | operate | new |
| `skills/tmux-agents/scripts/tmux_agent.py` | script | start, send, keys, read, wait, run, ls, kill, socket on a private tmux socket, one per project | build / test | new |
| `skills/secrets-hygiene/templates/` | template | `.gitignore` block, `.env.example`, `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, plain git hook (install it with `scan_secrets.py` beside it), GitHub Actions secret scan | build | new |
| `skills/scheduled-agents/templates/` | template | crontab lines (job and deadman), LaunchAgent plists for the job and its deadman, Task Scheduler PowerShell (both tasks), GitHub Actions workflow | operate | new |

**Maturity labels.** "proven" means the skill is generalized from a tool or runbook that runs in production in our own harness today. "new" means it was written for this marketplace from documentation and best practice and has unit tests, but has not yet been battle-tested in production. Where a skill mixes both, the table says which part is which.

Notes on the "proven" labels, so you can weigh them:

- `add-auth` and `scale-10k` are lightly edited from skills installed in our harness. The decision trees and audit checklists are what we use; we have not run every provider path ourselves. Provider prices and APIs change, so the skills tell the agent to check the pricing page and the installed framework version.
- `cheap-llm-routing`: the rules (privacy bar, forced tool call, key-prefix gate, paid fallback) come from a production feature that moved a structured matching task to a free tier. The bundled router script is new.
- `scheduled-agents`: the guard patterns (success-only logging, content-timestamp deadman, alert-delivery check, launchd env gotcha) run in our harness daily. The Windows and GitHub Actions templates and both scripts are new.
- `tmux-agents`: the pattern drives our parallel agent runs. The helper script is new.

## How to use each item

### add-auth

Ask: "add sign-in to this app", or run `/foundry-builder-kit:add-auth` (optionally with `clerk`, `supabase`, `better-auth`, `authjs`, or `--dry-run`). The agent audits first, recommends one provider with the trade-off, asks before changing code, then verifies: build passes, an anonymous request to a protected route is redirected, sign-out works, `.env.local` is gitignored.

### scale-10k

Ask: "is this ready for launch?" or run `/foundry-builder-kit:scale-10k` (or `scale-10k rate-limiting`, `--audit-only`, `--cost-estimate`). You get a READY / NEEDS WORK / CRITICAL scorecard with file and line citations, a cost table at 1k, 5k, 10k and 50k users, and fixes in priority order.

### secrets-hygiene

Ask: "set up secret scanning" or "I committed my OpenAI key". Prevention takes about 10 minutes: gitignore block, `.env.example`, gitleaks pre-commit hook, CI scan. For a leak, the order is: probe the key, map every place it is used, mint a new one, swap all consumers, revoke the old one, probe again until it reports DEAD, and only then scrub git history.

```bash
LEAKED=sk-... python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/secrets-hygiene/scripts/probe_key.py" openai:LEAKED
```

### Commit secret guard (hook)

Enabled automatically with the plugin. It looks at every Bash command, ignores everything except `git commit`, and blocks the commit (with redacted findings) when what the commit WILL contain looks like a key: what is already staged, plus whatever the same command stages first. That covers `git add -A && git commit`, `git add . ; git commit`, `git add <file> && git commit`, `git add -f .env && git commit`, `git commit -a` / `-am` / `git commit <paths>`, and `git init && git add . && git commit`, across `&&`, `||`, `;`, pipes, newlines and subshells, with redirections (`2>/dev/null`, `2>&1 | tail`), `# comments` and heredocs read the way the shell reads them. It follows `cd`, `pushd`, `git -C DIR`, `bash -c '...'`, `eval`, runners such as `timeout`, `sudo`, `xargs` and `find -exec`, and git aliases (`git ci`, `!shell` aliases). A path known only at run time (`"$FILE"`, `$(...)`) counts as the whole tree. The command text is scanned too, so a key in a commit message, or in a file the same command writes with `echo` or a heredoc, is caught. The index is always scanned with the bundled scanner, and also with gitleaks when it is installed, so the verdict is the same whether a file was staged earlier or by this command; files the command is about to stage are scanned with the bundled scanner (untracked files over 2 MB are skipped, symlinks count as links, not as the file they point to). A command that copies a key in from outside the repo and commits it in the same call (`cp ~/key.pem . && git add . && git commit`) cannot be seen before it runs: the git pre-commit hook covers that. If the guard itself hits an error it lets the command run.

It guards commits the agent makes; install the git pre-commit hook from `secrets-hygiene` for the commits you type. Turn it off for a session by starting Claude Code with it off: `export FOUNDRY_COMMIT_SECRET_GUARD=0` in your terminal, then `claude` (an `export` the agent runs in its Bash tool does not reach the hook). The old name `FOUNDRY_SECRETS_GUARD=0` still works but is deprecated. Not the same switch as `FOUNDRY_SECRET_GUARD` (singular), which belongs to the foundry-guardrails plugin's secret-guard hook. Mark a deliberate fake with the comment `secrets-hygiene: allow` (or `gitleaks:allow`; each is honored by both scanners). Obvious placeholders (`sk-ant-your-key-here`, `ghp_xxxx...`, a value marked FAKE), AWS's documentation key `AKIA...EXAMPLE` and database URLs on `localhost` are not flagged.

### cheap-llm-routing

Ask: "make this classification call free" or "use Groq for this, with a fallback". Mark each call `private` (real user data) or `public`. Private data never goes to a provider whose terms allow training on inputs.

```bash
python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/cheap-llm-routing/scripts/structured_router.py" --schema schema.json --data-class private --plan
```

No keys yet? `--mock-response mock.json` runs the full call path offline (privacy bar, forced tool call, validation, fall-through); the skill's `examples/` folder has a plain and a fall-through mock.

### scheduled-agents

Ask: "run this agent every morning" or "why did my cron job stop". The agent writes the job as one foreground turn, wraps it with `run_headless.py`, and schedules TWO entries from the templates: the job and a separate `deadman.py check`, so a silent stop becomes an alert. Under cron and launchd the deadman reads its webhook URL from a file (`--webhook-file`), because those schedulers do not see variables from your shell profile. With no working channel it exits 3, prints `NO ALERT CHANNEL`, and writes `<name>.DEADMAN-ALERT.txt` next to the heartbeat.

### tmux-agents

Ask: "keep the dev server running while you test" or "drive this REPL". The agent uses `tmux_agent.py` to start a named session, wait for a prompt, send input, read output, and clean up. Each project gets its own socket (keyed on the git top-level), so agents in different projects never share or kill each other's sessions; set `TMUX_AGENT_SOCKET` to share one on purpose.

## Install one item on its own

Every skill is self-contained: its scripts, templates and examples live inside its own folder and are referenced through `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}`, so you can copy one folder without the rest of the plugin.

```bash
cp -R skills/secrets-hygiene ~/.claude/skills/        # personal, every project
cp -R skills/secrets-hygiene .claude/skills/          # this project only
```

- Standalone: `add-auth`, `scale-10k`, `cheap-llm-routing`, `scheduled-agents`, `tmux-agents`, `secrets-hygiene`. Each works when copied on its own.
- Needs a skill: no agents ship in this plugin, so nothing depends on another item.
- Plugin only: the commit secret guard hook. Copying `secrets-hygiene` brings the scanner and the guard script, but nothing runs the guard on agent commits unless the plugin is installed. Without the plugin, install the git pre-commit hook from `secrets-hygiene` instead.

## Requirements

- Claude Code with plugin support.
- Python 3.9+ on PATH as `python3` (scripts are stdlib only). On Windows, if your Python is `py` or `python`, the hook will not find `python3`; create an alias or install Python from python.org with the "add to PATH" option, or use WSL.
- `git` for the secret scanner and hook.
- Optional: `gitleaks` (recommended, `brew install gitleaks` or a release binary), `tmux` for `tmux-agents` (macOS, Linux, or WSL), and accounts with whichever auth, LLM, and email providers you choose.

## Tests

From this plugin directory:

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

The tmux tests are skipped when tmux is not installed; the gitleaks test is skipped when gitleaks is not installed. No test touches the network.

## Related

For a fuller team harness (memory, hooks, team skills) see the cohort's agent team kit: https://github.com/ai-foundry-byu/agent-team-kit

## License

MIT. The tmux send-text-then-Enter timing follows the tmux skill from the OpenClaw project (MIT); the helper here is a fresh implementation.
